papers.abstract: Necrosis is a defining feature and an active hypoxic niche implicated in immune escape and treatment resistance in glioblastoma (GBM). We asked whether MRI-defined necrosis morphology is associated with circulating immune profiles and overall survival (OS). We retrospectively studied 111 patients with newly diagnosed IDH-wildtype GBM resected in 2018-2024. Preoperative necrosis was classified visually as classic confluent or multiloculated. Two blinded readers reclassified all cases independently. Immune subsets were assessed by flow cytometry (n = 59, 48/11 classic/multiloculated) and plasma cytokines by multiplex immunoassay (n = 54, 45/9). All 28 immune analytes were exploratory, corrected across the panel. OS from surgery was analyzed with Kaplan-Meier and Cox models, including treatment and small-sample sensitivity analyses. Inter-reader agreement was kappa = 0.883. Multiloculated morphology was associated with longer OS (median, 17.4 vs. 14.4 months; HR, 0.55, 95% CI, 0.31-0.98, p = 0.041), including after multivariable adjustment (n = 94; HR, 0.42, 0.22-0.81, p = 0.010; Firth-penalized, 0.44, p = 0.007), exclusion of untreated patients and early deaths, and restriction to completed chemoradiation (HR, 0.37, 0.16-0.84, p = 0.018). Classic morphology was associated with fewer conventional dendritic cells (cDCs) (0.15% vs. 0.41%, p = 0.006), more mature natural killer cells (p = 0.022), and lower granzyme B, IL-2, IL-4, IL-6, and IL-10, but no difference survived correction (lowest q = 0.088). Multiloculated patients were younger (57.2 vs. 64.3 years, p = 0.032). The cDC association did not persist after adjustment for deep-seated location (p = 0.124). Multiloculated necrosis was associated with longer OS after adjustment for established prognostic factors, which requires external validation. Circulating immune differences were exploratory and could not be separated from tumor location. Not applicable.

papers.abstract: Circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) fragmentation patterns provide a promising source of molecular information for liquid biopsy applications. However, the sequence features underlying fragmentation and their relationship to tumour-derived DNA remain incompletely understood. Here, we characterized fragment-end sequence signatures of extracellular cfDNA across cell lines, extracellular compartments, stress conditions and plasma from patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). cfDNA derived from cell lines was characterized using Oxford Nanopore sequencing, followed by fragment-end analysis. Publicly available Nanopore cfDNA datasets from healthy individuals and NSCLC patients were analyzed to examine dinucleotide patterns and derive a motif ratio index. These signatures were further assessed for their association with estimated ctDNA abundance in an independent cohort of 50 EGFR-mutant NSCLC patients. Nanopore sequencing of A549, H460 and WI38 cell-line cfDNA revealed reproducible end-motif patterns, with enrichment of AT-, GT- and CT-containing termini. Analysis of plasma cfDNA from healthy individuals showed distinct end-motif profiles from cell-line-derived cfDNA, with separation maintained after reducing 4-mer motifs to 5'-terminal dinucleotide features. An exploratory motif ratio based on these patterns showed a modest increase in lung cancer patients compared with healthy individuals. In an independent Illumina cohort of 50 NSCLC patients with activating EGFR mutations, 5'-terminal dinucleotide frequencies were associated with estimated circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) abundance using cross-validated LASSO (Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator) regression (Spearman ρ = .73, p = 3.35 × 10‒9). The predefined motif ratio showed a strong correlation with estimated ctDNA concentration (Spearman ρ = .76, p = 1.89 × 10‒10). These findings suggest that simple, interpretable cfDNA end-motif signatures capture sequence features associated with ctDNA abundance and warrant further validation for non-invasive cancer monitoring.

papers.abstract: Serum C-reactive protein (CRP) and faecal calprotectin, used to monitor inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) between endoscopies, require intermittent blood or stool sampling. We assessed whether a skin-worn perspiration sensor could measure CRP and calprotectin continuously; TNFα and IL-6 were exploratory analytes. At three US centres, perspiration biomarkers were recorded continuously for 3-30 days in 52 IBD patients (27 ulcerative colitis, 24 Crohn's disease, 1 indeterminate colitis) and 19-32 days in 9 controls, with serum CRP and faecal calprotectin sampled at baseline and study end. Agreement was assessed using correlation and Bland-Altman analysis; ROC-derived cutoffs matched serum CRP 5 mg/L and faecal 250 µg/g. Circadian rhythmicity and ultradian (4-12 h) power were compared among biochemically active IBD (serum CRP > 5 mg/L; n = 15), inactive (n = 37), and controls. 47 of 52 IBD participants (90.4%) completed the protocol. Across 99 paired observations, perspiration CRP correlated with serum CRP (r = .52-.58); perspiration and faecal calprotectin correlated in ulcerative colitis (r = .59-.62) but not in Crohn's disease. A perspiration CRP cutoff of 1551 pg/mL (serum 5 mg/L) gave 85.7% sensitivity and 89.4% specificity; a calprotectin cutoff of 385 (µg/g)·min (faecal 250 µg/g) gave 92.3% and 67.9%. Negative predictive values were high (95%-97%), positive modest (57%). Circadian MESOR and amplitude of both markers were higher in active than inactive IBD. Ultradian power differed by group for calprotectin (Kruskal-Wallis p = .0005) and CRP (p = .0037)-highest in active disease, lowest in controls-but the active-inactive difference was non-significant after false-discovery-rate correction. Perspiration CRP agreed moderately with serum CRP, and perspiration calprotectin with faecal calprotectin in ulcerative colitis only. Their high negative predictive values support the study as a non-invasive adjunct to, not a substitute for, standard-of-care testing. All findings are preliminary, and the temporal-dynamics results are hypothesis-generating, needing confirmation in a larger, prospectively designed, endoscopy-anchored cohort.

papers.abstract: The recently described lactyltransferase activity of alanyl-tRNA synthetase 1 (AARS1) raises questions about its metabolic functions in hepatocellular carcinoma. We examined phosphoglycerate dehydrogenase (PHGDH) as a potential lactylation substrate linking AARS1 to serine metabolism and tumour growth. Public expression data and patient tissues were studied alongside proteomic, lactylomic and targeted metabolomic profiles. Cellular and xenograft experiments used gene depletion, overexpression and reconstitution with wild-type or mutant proteins. Immunoprecipitation and activity measurements assessed PHGDH regulation. Survival was examined with Kaplan‒Meier estimates and Cox regression, while experimental groups were compared by t-tests or analysis of variance. Of 140 paired specimens, 119 tumours (85%) had higher AARS1 mRNA than their non-tumour counterparts. Elevated AARS1 independently predicted poorer survival, and E2F4 depletion lowered AARS1 expression. AARS1 supported malignant phenotypes, lactate production and PHGDH lactylation. Mass spectrometry detected lactylation at PHGDH-K394. Relative to wild-type PHGDH, K394R showed less lactylation and supported lower lysate enzyme activity, serine, glycine and glutathione levels. The mutant also increased reactive oxygen species, provided weaker phenotypic rescue and supported less xenograft growth. Depleting AARS1 reduced enzyme activity and malignant phenotypes in the wild-type background; no further significant reduction was detected with K394R. β-Alanine inhibited xenograft growth, but PHGDH-K394 alone could not account for its effects. AARS1-associated PHGDH-K394 lactylation may connect serine metabolism and redox regulation to hepatocellular carcinoma progression. Establishing therapeutic relevance will require site-specific mechanistic experiments and additional preclinical validation.

papers.abstract: Male breast cancer (MBC) represents a small proportion of all breast cancer (BC) cases, yet it is characterized by a higher rate of lymph node metastasis and poorer prognosis compared to female breast cancer (FBC). However, limited research has been conducted on MBC primarily due to its rarity and the technological constraints. To address this, we performed single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) on samples from 16 MBC patients (87 518 cells) and imaging mass cytometry (IMC) on samples from 42 patients (265 137 cells), enabling a comprehensive analysis of the MBC microenvironment at both single-cell transcriptome and protein levels. At the autosomal level, the MBC tumor cells and their microenvironment exhibit distinct characteristics. We found that PDZ binding kinase (PBK) expression was elevated in MBC tumor cells and linked to proliferation-related programs, whereas SRY-Box transcription factor 4 (SOX4) expression was increased in endothelial cells and associated with endothelial-mesenchymal transition (EndMT) signatures and metastatic potential. Additionally, IMC analysis revealed notable differences in the spatial features of the tumor microenvironment between MBC and FBC. Regarding sex-chromosomal regulation, the lysine demethylase 5D (KDM5D) gene originating from the Y chromosome was associated with cGAS/STING protein abundance and reduced immune cell infiltration in MBC. In conclusion, both autosomal and sex-chromosomal regulation may collectively contribute to the modulation of microenvironmental differences between MBC and FBC. Whether KDM5D is functionally linked to cGAS/STING signaling requires further validation. Our findings provide insights into the unique microenvironment and clinical manifestations of MBC and generate hypotheses for future functional studies. Multi-omics profiling reveals a distinct, relatively immune-cold microenvironment in male breast cancer. PBK expression is associated with proliferation programs in MBC epithelial cells. SOX4 expression in endothelial cells is linked to an EndMT-like phenotype. KDM5D-low status is associated with reduced cGAS/STING protein levels and immune infiltration.

papers.abstract: Sepsis-induced myocardial dysfunction (SIMD) is a key contributor to death among individuals with sepsis. Serpina3n (a serine protease inhibitor) contributes critically to various cardiovascular diseases. However, whether Serpina3n is involved in SIMD and its underlying mechanisms remain unclear. A SIMD model was established by either an intraperitoneal injection of lipopolysaccharide (LPS) or caecal ligation and puncture (CLP) in mice. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) was carried out to examine Serpina3n expression and its cellular localisation in mouse hearts. Serpina3n expression was also examined in LPS-treated neonatal mouse cardiac fibroblasts (NMCFs) and neonatal mouse cardiomyocytes (NMCMs). Global Serpina3n knockout (KO) (Serpina3n-/-) and fibroblast-specific Serpina3n-deficient (Serpina3nflox/flox, Col1a2-iCre) mouse models were used for functional validation in vivo. Serpina3n expression was notably up-regulated in the hearts of SIMD mice, and it was enriched mainly in cardiac fibroblasts (CFs). Consistent with the scRNA-seq data, Serpina3n expression was markedly increased in LPS-treated NMCFs but not in NMCMs. Furthermore, both global Serpina3n KO and fibroblast-specific Serpina3n deletion exacerbated cardiac inflammation and dysfunction, facilitated the progression of SIMD and ultimately increased mortality. Mechanistically, LPS stimulation promoted the secretion of Serpina3n from CFs, which acted on cardiomyocytes (CMs) in a paracrine manner, thereby attenuating the expression of proteins related to the Janus kinase/signal transducer and activator of transcription signalling pathway and reducing cardiac inflammatory cell infiltration to ultimately exert a cardioprotective effect. These processes were disrupted by fibroblast-specific Serpina3n deficiency. Collectively, these findings indicate that CF-derived Serpina3n mediates CF-CM crosstalk and plays an essential protective role in SIMD, providing mechanistic insights and a potential candidate target for further preclinical investigations of SIMD.

papers.abstract: Impaired fertility can occur as a late effect of childhood cancer treatment. This study aimed to assess the prevalence and predictors of fertility-related distress in young adult childhood cancer survivors, compared to a general population sample. This nationwide, population-based cross-sectional study included 1333 women (67% response rate) and 1213 men (54%) aged 19-40, who had been treated for cancer in Sweden between ages 0 and 17. Eligible survivors were identified through the National Quality Registry for Childhood Cancer in Sweden. A comparison group was randomly selected from the Swedish Population Registry, comprising 493 (51% response rate) women and 326 (34%) men. The study combined clinical registry data and self-report measures. The main outcome was high fertility-related distress assessed with the six-dimension Reproductive Concerns After Cancer (RCAC) scale, with high distress defined as a mean score above 4. The comparison group completed only the three RCAC dimensions relevant to adults without a history of cancer. Group comparisons were undertaken using logistic regression, with analyses stratified by sex. A total of 44% of female and 23% of male survivors reported high fertility-related distress in at least one RCAC dimension. Distress was most prevalent in the Fertility potential dimension, and both female and male survivors were significantly more likely to report high distress regarding fertility potential than women and men in the comparison group. Among survivors, high fertility-related distress across several RCAC dimensions was associated with not having children, the desire for (additional) children, having undergone intensive cancer treatments or fertility-preservation procedures, receiving ongoing hormone replacement therapy, and experiencing concurrent anxiety and depressive symptoms. The results underscore the need to address fertility-related concerns in the follow-up care of childhood cancer survivors.

papers.abstract: Central adiposity, captured by the weight-adjusted-waist index (WWI), may correlate with breast cancer risk, but whether the association persists after adjustment for demographic and cardiometabolic confounders remains unclear. We examined the cross-sectional association between WWI and breast cancer prevalence in U.S. adult women. Using National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 1999-2016 data (n = 6782; 208 breast-cancer cases), we fit survey-weighted logistic models with three levels of covariate adjustment, restricted cubic splines (RCS), and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost)-based variable importance. Propensity-score matching (PSM) and sensitivity analyses were performed. After adjustment for age, race, poverty-to-income ratio (PIR), hypertension, diabetes, and coronary heart disease (CHD), the highest vs. lowest WWI quartile showed an odds ratio (OR) of 1.84 (95% CI 1.19-2.91; p = 0.008). In Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis of the full analytic cohort (n = 6782), age dominated variable importance (mean |SHAP| 0.0071), followed by race (0.0016) and WWI (0.0015); this ordering was stable across repeated subsample replicates. RCS showed a significant linear association (p overall = 0.008), with an exploratory inflection near WWI ≈12.4. Higher WWI was associated with lower estradiol (E2) and sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG) and a higher total testosterone (TT)-to-SHBG ratio. WWI was cross-sectionally associated with breast cancer prevalence after adjustment for age, race, PIR, hypertension, diabetes, and CHD, supporting its potential role as a simple marker of central adiposity in descriptive epidemiology.

papers.abstract: Although allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) offers curative potential for several hematologic malignancies, it is associated with a substantial psychological burden. However, prospective studies simultaneously evaluating psychological distress, quality of life, unmet needs, caregiver strain, and baseline psychosocial vulnerability remain limited. We therefore conducted a prospective single-center observational study of 115 adult allo-HSCT recipients assessed peri-transplant (T0), and at 6 (T1) and 12 (T2) months. Thirty-two caregivers provided at least one Family Strain Questionnaire-Short Form response, and 31 completed all items required for score calculation. The Psychosocial Assessment of Candidates for Transplantation (PACT) was available for 80 patients and was analyzed exploratorily because the Italian version has not undergone formal psychometric validation. Scores were generally favorable (median score: 38), with only nine patients classified as having low psychosocial suitability (PACT score ≤ 29). Clinically relevant distress (Distress Thermometer ≥ 4) was observed in 67.5%, 69.7%, and 47.4% of patients with valid data at T0, T1, and T2, respectively. Psychological Distress Inventory scores were higher at 6 months than at T0; the 12-month estimate was numerically lower than at 6 months, but neither the T1-T2 nor the T0-T2 contrast was statistically significant. Informational and communication needs remained frequent, while several SF-36 domains worsened at 6 months and improved at 12 months. Mean caregiver strain score did not change significantly over time; however, more than half of assessed caregivers were classified in areas indicating that psychological support was strongly recommended or urgent at each time point. These findings indicate distinct psychosocial trajectories among participants and support the potential value of repeated multidimensional psychosocial assessment during the first year after allo-HSCT.

papers.abstract: The albumin-bilirubin (ALBI) score measures hepatic reserve in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). We evaluated the association between longitudinal ALBI changes during immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy and overall survival (OS), including their prognostic contribution beyond baseline ALBI. This retrospective cohort included 227 patients receiving ICI-based therapy. Serial ALBI trajectory was assessable in 217 patients. Cox regression, patient-clustered time-dependent analyses, 42-, 84-, and 168-day landmarks, and endpoint sensitivity analyses were performed. Of 227 patients, 217 met the serial-ALBI criteria (149 deaths in the primary analysis). Non-Decliner, Slow Decliner, and Rapid Decliner groups numbered 98, 61, and 58; median OS was 24.8, 11.5, and 4.8 months. Rapid Decliner versus Non-Decliner adjusted hazard ratio (HR) was 4.21 (95% confidence interval [CI] 2.70-6.57) and 4.71 (2.98-7.44) after baseline ALBI adjustment. At day 84 (n = 185; 123 events), adjusted HR was 2.44 (1.51-3.92). Apparent C-index increased from 0.601 to 0.643 (approximately 0.04); this modest in-sample gain was not validated. Worsening longitudinal ALBI was associated with shorter survival in this retrospective HCC cohort, with attenuation in later landmark analyses. The exploratory 180-day trajectory groups are defined after treatment begins; their Cox HRs summarize associations over follow-up rather than constant relative hazards. Continuous-slope estimates were sensitive to extreme observations. Prospective short-window derivation and independent validation are required before clinical use.

papers.abstract: Cancer outcome disparities due to Australian rurality are a public health concern, to which inequities in health literacy may contribute. In response, public health campaigns have focused on promoting early symptom awareness and timely help-seeking. This study examined how the Find Cancer Early campaign was perceived by rural Western Australians. Using a convergent parallel mixed methods design, quantitative and qualitative data were collected concurrently through annual computer-assisted telephone interviews (2018-2021) with adults aged ≥ 40 years in rural and regional Western Australia, recruited via landline and mobile numbers from residential telephone databases. Survey items assessed campaign exposure, attitudes towards symptom awareness campaigns, and campaign perceptions. Exposure was measured by combining open-ended recall with prompted recognition of television, radio, online, and print materials. Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive statistics and short-answer descriptions of recalled advertising using inductive thematic analysis. Of 5088 surveyed rural Western Australians, 3416 (67.1%) recalled or recognised the Find Cancer Early campaign. Perceptions of the campaign were generally favourable, particularly regarding clarity, credibility, and relevance. Thematic analysis identified three themes: 'Rural Doctors and Regional Champions' (recall of specific campaign phases), 'Pieces of the Message' (fragmented recall of campaign messages), and 'Contextual Influences' (the influence of broader media on recall and interpretation). The Find Cancer Early campaign achieved high awareness of campaign exposure and was perceived positively. However, participants often recalled specific symptoms or contextual elements rather than the campaign's call to action. The findings provide insight into how rural Western Australians interpret early symptom awareness campaigns and may inform future campaigns.

papers.abstract: Although the Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index (GNRI) was initially developed for geriatric nutritional assessment and has been validated as a prognostic tool in various populations, its prognostic implications, specifically in patients with cancer admitted to the ICU, remain limited. Data for adult ICU patients with cancer were extracted from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care (MIMIC)-IV and the eICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU-CRD). GNRI was calculated using serum albumin levels and body weight, and patients were stratified into nutritional risk categories: low-risk (GNRI ≥ 82) and high-risk (GNRI < 82). Primary outcomes were in-hospital mortality and 1-year mortality. Multivariable logistic and Cox regression models were used to assess associations between GNRI and mortality. The nonlinear relationships were examined using restricted cubic splines. A total of 4006 ICU patients with cancer were analyzed: 1664 from the MIMIC-IV database and 2342 from the eICU-CRD database. The median GNRI was 78.0 (interquartile range [IQR]: 69.8-86.4) in MIMIC-IV and 73.0 (IQR: 63.7-82.5) in eICU-CRD, with 63.4% and 74.5% of patients classified as high nutritional risk, respectively. In both cohorts, a high GNRI risk was significantly associated with increased in-hospital mortality (MIMIC-IV: 30.3% vs. 17.4%; eICU-CRD: 23.8% vs. 10.7%) and, in MIMIC-IV, with higher 1-year mortality (64.2% vs. 48.6%). Multivariable analysis confirmed that each 1-unit increase in GNRI was independently associated with reduced in-hospital mortality (MIMIC-IV: OR 0.973, 95% CI 0.963-0.983; eICU-CRD: OR 0.971, 95% CI 0.963-0.980) and 1-year mortality (HR 0.980, 95% CI 0.975-0.986). Restricted cubic spline analyses revealed a nearly linear inverse relationship between GNRI and mortality risk. GNRI was independently associated with both short- and long-term mortality in ICU patients with cancer, highlighting its potential as a simple, objective marker of nutritional risk and prognosis. These findings are observational, and whether GNRI-guided nutritional interventions improve outcomes warrants prospective evaluation.

papers.abstract: The prognostic significance of adverse pathological features in urothelial carcinoma of the bladder (UCB) remains incompletely understood, particularly in patients with early-onset disease. This study compared survival between early-onset (< 50 years) and non-early-onset (≥ 50 years) UCB patients to evaluate the prognostic significance of adverse features in the early-onset cohort. We retrospectively analyzed 2686 UCB patients who underwent radical cystectomy between 1993 and 2025. Patients were classified according to the age at diagnosis. Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed to improve the comparability of measured clinicopathological characteristics between the two groups. Overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) were estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method. Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to evaluate prognostic factors in the early-onset cohort. After 1:1 PSM, 143 matched pairs were analyzed. Early-onset patients had better OS (hazard ratio [HR], 0.63; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.43-0.94; log-rank p = 0.028) and PFS (HR, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.45-0.96; log-rank p = 0.028) than matched non-early-onset patients. Among the 155 early-onset patients, 42 deaths occurred. In the univariable analysis, advanced T stage, N stage, sarcomatoid subtype, squamous/glandular differentiation, and lymphovascular invasion were associated with worse OS. After multivariable analysis, advanced T stage (adjusted HR, 2.86; 95% CI, 1.05-7.81), N stage (adjusted HR, 3.34; 95% CI, 1.65-6.77), and sarcomatoid subtype (adjusted HR, 2.82; 95% CI, 1.20-6.66) remained independently associated with worse OS. Early-onset UCB was associated with better OS and PFS than non-early-onset UCB after PSM. However, advanced T stage, N stage, and sarcomatoid subtype identified a high-risk subgroup among younger patients. These findings highlight the need for risk-adapted management in younger patients.

papers.abstract: Currently, immunochemotherapy is the standard first-line treatment for extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC). However, all recommended second-line strategies have been investigated prior to the advent of immunotherapy, and real-world data on the subsequent treatment landscape in ES-SCLC after disease progression on first-line immunochemotherapy remain limited. To characterize the landscape and evaluate clinical outcomes of distinct second-line treatment regimens in patients with ES-SCLC who experienced disease progression following first-line immunochemotherapy in real-world practice. We retrospectively enrolled 94 patients with ES-SCLC who progressed after first-line immunochemotherapy and received second-line treatment between February 2020 and February 2024. Eligible patients were divided into three groups based on their second-line treatment regimens: the chemotherapy-alone (C) group, the immunochemotherapy (CI) group, and the anti-angiogenic-containing therapy (AT) group. Kaplan-Meier (K-M) method was applied to compare the survival outcomes. Multivariate Cox regression analyses were conducted to identify independent predictors. Further exploratory subgroup analyses stratified by platinum-free interval (PFI) were performed. The median progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) for all enrolled patients were 3.77 months and 9.80 months, respectively. Patients in the AT group exhibited the shortest PFS and OS compared to patients in the C group and CI group. Multivariate Cox proportional-hazards regression revealed that adrenal progression pattern was an independent adverse prognostic factor for PFS, whereas AT therapy was independently associated with worse OS. Exploratory subgroup analysis based on PFI showed no significant survival differences among the three treatment groups. For ES-SCLC patients progressing after first-line immunochemotherapy, second-line AT is associated with inferior OS, but this may reflect treatment selection bias rather than anti-angiogenic therapy itself. Moreover, regardless of PFI status, no significant differences in survival outcomes were observed among patients receiving different treatment regimens; thus, clinical trials should be recommended for patients receiving second-line therapy.

papers.abstract: Tumor angiogenesis is sustained not only by endothelial activation but also by adaptive reprogramming of the perivascular niche. Tetraspanin Kai1 (CD82) functions as a pericyte-intrinsic suppressor of angiogenic activation, yet the mechanisms underlying its loss within angiogenic tumor microenvironments remain poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that PDGF-BB and basic fibroblast growth factor (bFGF), but not VEGF-A, reduce Kai1 expression in murine pericyte-like model. Mechanistically, PDGFR/FGFR signaling is associated with a dual-layer regulatory program: (1) Src-sensitive increases in DNMT1 and DNMT3A are associated with increased Kai1 promoter methylation and reduced transcription; and (2) PKC-sensitive, Flotillin-1-associated trafficking contributes to Kai1 internalization and lysosomal degradation. Functionally, DNMT inhibition or lysosomal blockade restored Kai1 levels and attenuated growth factor-induced sprout outgrowth in 3D spheroids. In vivo, combined DNMT and lysosomal inhibition reduced tumor growth in WT mice, whereas a comparable reduction was not observed in Kai1 KO mice. Collectively, our findings identify a growth factor-programmed "off-switch" that disables a pericyte-intrinsic anti-angiogenic brake. These findings nominate pericyte Kai1 regulation as a potential mechanism for future investigation in VEGF-independent vascular remodeling.

papers.abstract: Postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs) importantly contribute to postoperative morbidity and mortality, particularly for patients classified American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) Physical Status III. Whether PPC risk factors depend on sex remains unclear. We hypothesize that sex modifies the relationship between perioperative risk factors and PPCs in patients assigned an ASA III status undergoing noncardiothoracic surgery with general anesthesia. We performed a secondary analysis of prospective data from 1,202 patients undergoing noncardiothoracic surgery. We collected data on preoperative patient demographics, comorbidities, intraoperative physiology, medications, and procedure information. The primary outcome was a composite of PPCs by postoperative day 7. Mixed-effects linear models incorporated sex as main and interaction effect. Age, upper abdominal surgery, and surgical duration significantly increased the odds of ≥ 1 PPC by postoperative day 7. Male patients presented a higher rate of ≥ 3 PPCs, and female patients received higher tidal volumes per predicted body weight and driving pressures. Sex did not significantly modify the relationship between perioperative factors and the primary outcome (no P < 0.05 for the interaction with sex). In the secondary analysis, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) affected atelectasis more strongly in male than in female patients (relative odds ratio for female vs male patients, 0.27; 95% confidence interval, 0.13 to 0.57). In patients classified ASA III undergoing noncardiothoracic surgery with general anesthesia, perioperative factors are predominantly not modified by sex in their relationship to PPCs. The association between GERD and atelectasis in male patients could be explored in future prospective studies as a target for reducing PPCs.

papers.abstract: We sought to conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis with the primary objective to identify prognostic factors associated with developing a catheter-related thrombosis in the critical care setting. Our secondary objective was to report the incidence of this entity. We searched, MEDLINE® and Embase® from inception through 4 May 2024 for all studies in patients with critical illness that reported catheter-related thrombosis, with an updated search performed on 23 October 2025. We included English-language studies that described prognostic factors for developing a catheter-related thrombosis or reported the incidence of this complication in the critical care setting. Two authors performed citation screening and data extraction. We pooled adjusted odds ratios (aORs) and adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) separately for prognostic factors using a random-effects model and inverse variance weighting. Risk of bias for individual studies was evaluated using the Quality in Prognosis Studies tool. We assessed certainty of evidence using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluations approach. We included 32 studies involving 11,943 patients. Identified prognostic variables with a moderate- or high-certainty association for developing a catheter-related thrombosis include increasing age (aOR per 10-yr increase, 1.16; 95% CI, 1.06 to 1.27; three studies; 1,594 patients; high certainty), trauma-related admission (aOR, 1.48; 95% CI, 0.93 to 2.34; three studies; 3,089 patients; high certainty), surgical-related admission (aOR, 2.50; 95% CI, 1.77 to 3.52; three studies; 2,208 patients; aHR, 1.35; 95% CI, 0.60 to 3.02; two studies; 297 patients; high certainty), internal jugular insertion site as compared with other insertion sites (aOR, 3.76; 95% CI, 2.82 to 5.01; four studies; 4,681 patients; high certainty), single/double-lumen as compared with more lumens (aOR, 1.61; 95% CI, 0.82 to 3.13; three studies; 1,594 patients; moderate certainty), and peripheral insertion site (aOR, 2.30; 95% CI, 0.74 to 7.08; two studies; 264 patients; moderate certainty). The median incidence of catheter-related thrombosis was 13.3% [interquartile range, 3.7%-31.3%]. In this systematic review and meta-analysis, we found that increasing age, surgical type admissions, large catheters, and factors potentially related with catheter duration were associated with developing a catheter-related thrombosis in the critical care setting. Furthermore, we identified significant variation in the reported rates of catheter-related thrombosis, with an average rate of approximately 1 in every 8 patients. When these identified risk factors are present, clinicians may consider more aggressive thromboprophylaxis regimens to better tailor prevention strategies to individual patient risk profiles. papers.abstract: Endocrine therapy (ET) reduces recurrence and improves survival in patients with hormone receptor-positive breast cancer (BC), yet many patients are nonadherent. The impact of health-related social needs (HRSN) on ET nonadherence remains poorly understood. We extracted electronic health record data on patients with nonmetastatic BC followed at NewYork-Presbyterian/Columbia University Irving Medical Center. Patients were eligible if they were adults, prescribed ET, and screened for HRSN (food insecurity, housing instability, transportation needs). ET nonadherence during the 6 months after HRSN screening was determined using proportion of days covered (PDC), with PDC < 80% considered nonadherent. Logistic regression models estimated associations between each HRSN and ET nonadherence, adjusting for demographics, BC characteristics, medication count, and comorbidities. We identified 960 eligible BC patients between January 2022 and October 2024 (median age 67 [IQR 58-75] years, 99% female, 12% Black, 41% Hispanic, 38% non-English speaking, 67% publicly insured, 63% stage 0-I BC, 18% tamoxifen use, 13% chemotherapy use, 80% prescribed ≥ 3 medications). Overall, 275 (29%) patients were nonadherent to ET; 15% reported food insecurity, 10% housing instability, and 6% transportation needs. In adjusted analyses, housing instability (OR 1.97, 95% CI 1.11-3.46, p = 0.02) and transportation needs (OR 3.43, 95% CI 1.69-7.07, p < 0.01), but not food insecurity (OR 1.40, 95% CI 0.89-2.19, p = 0.15) were significantly associated with ET nonadherence. Housing instability and transportation needs were independently associated with higher odds of ET nonadherence in our sample. Screening for and addressing HRSN may represent an effective strategy for improving ET adherence and cancer-related outcomes.

papers.abstract: Grade 2 mIDH gliomas affect adults of working age and may disrupt everyday functioning, work capacity, and family life for many years. We assessed long-term socioeconomic, healthcare, and psychiatric burden among patients initially managed with active observation and their partners. This Danish nationwide observational matched cohort study included patients with incident grade 2 mIDH diffuse astrocytoma or oligodendroglioma diagnosed from 2010 to 2022. Patients receiving radiotherapy (RT) and/or chemotherapy (CT), palliative care, or dying within six months after diagnosis were excluded. Patients and partners were compared with coarsened exact matched population controls and outcomes were followed up to 10 years post-index and stratified by RT/CT treatment exposure. The study included 237 patients and 113 partners, matched to 1,161 patient controls and 550 partner controls. Ten-year overall patient survival was 72.7%. Patients experienced a profound and increasing burden: Over 10 years, they averaged - 163,000€ lost pay-check income and accumulated + 347,000€ combined incremental burden from public benefits, healthcare costs, and productivity loss (RT/CT-exposed: +513,000€, RT/CT unexposed: +163,000€) compared to controls. Partners maintained stable income and employment, but partners of RT/CT-exposed patients had increased work absence, averaging + 2.8 excess weeks annually (approximately twice the excess seen among partners of RT/CT-unexposed patients, + 1.4 weeks). Grade 2 IDH-mutant glioma imposes a significant, progressive long term multidimensional burden on patients and society. Disease progression and RT/CT initiation marks a clinically meaningful trajectory shift towards profoundly worse outcomes for patients and partners.

papers.abstract: Cytoreductive surgery (CRS) with hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (HIPEC) improves survival in selected patients with colorectal peritoneal metastases. However, outcomes remain heterogeneous, and tumor molecular biology may influence prognosis. We retrospectively reviewed patients with colorectal cancer and peritoneal metastases treated with CRS and HIPEC at Royal Hospital between May 2013 and August 2024. Patients were grouped by presence of genetic mutations (GM) versus no mutations (no-GM). Primary outcomes were overall survival (OS) and recurrence-free survival (RFS). Secondary outcomes included morbidity and prognostic factors for recurrence. Among 159 patients, 73 (45.9%) had a documented genetic mutation. Genetic mutation was associated with a shorter median RFS (8 months in the GM group vs. 27 months in the no-GM group; p 15 (HR 1.073; p = 0.005), and pre-HIPEC chemotherapy (HR 2.194; p = 0.003) were independently associated with recurrence. For OS, PCI (HR 1.066; p = 0.037) and poorly differentiated tumor grade (HR 2.946; p = 0.045) were independently associated with survival, whereas genetic mutation status was not (HR 1.477; p = 0.197). Genetic mutation was associated with shorter RFS after CRS and HIPEC, and this association persisted after multivariable adjustment. The association with OS was not independent of PCI and tumor grade, suggesting that disease burden may be the main driver of survival. Molecular status may complement established clinicopathological factors in patient assessment; larger prospective studies stratified by mutation type are needed.

papers.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy has transformed outcomes in patients with relapsed or refractory hematologic malignancies, yet clinical responses remain heterogeneous. Increasing evidence suggests that part of this variability may already be reflected before manufacturing, at the level of the leukapheresis starting material. This review highlights pre-apheresis T-cell fitness as an important upstream biological framework linking patient background to the quality of the starting material, manufacturing performance, and clinical efficacy. Available data indicate that the most informative attributes of high-quality starting material are defined not by T-cell number alone but by the preservation of early-differentiated T-cell subsets, maintenance of functional reserve, resilience to exhaustion-associated dysfunction, and metabolic adaptability. We discuss how prior treatment exposures, including chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and selected targeted agents, can influence these properties according to exposure type, dose intensity, treatment phase, and timing relative to leukapheresis. We further examine how host-related conditions, including immunosenescence, chronic infection, nutritional and metabolic imbalance, and high tumor burden, may alter precursor availability, reshape differentiation architecture, and impair T-cell functional competence before collection. Collectively, these observations support a shift from a quantitative view of leukapheresis products toward a biologically informed assessment of T-cell quality. Defining a favorable pre-collection window and establishing standardized pre-apheresis assessment strategies may therefore facilitate biologically informed leukapheresis planning and future optimization of CAR-T manufacturing and clinical outcomes.

papers.abstract: Young breast cancer survivors frequently seek guidance on whether pregnancy after treatment may increase their risk of recurrence. Observational studies addressing this question may be affected by healthy-mother selection and immortal-time bias if pregnancy timing is not appropriately considered. The source cohort included 419 women with breast cancer, including 79 with a documented post-diagnosis pregnancy. Each pregnancy case was matched without replacement to one to three eligible controls by age at diagnosis within 3 years and risk-set eligibility at the case-specific index year. The matched analysis included 79 cases and 142 controls in 79 sets. The primary Cox model was unweighted, stratified by matched set, used robust standard errors clustered by matched set, and adjusted for diagnosis year. A complementary full-cohort Cox model treated pregnancy as a time-dependent exposure. Thirty-nine disease-free survival events occurred after the matched index year. In the primary unweighted matched-set-stratified analysis adjusted for diagnosis year, pregnancy was associated with a lower estimated event hazard (hazard ratio [HR], 0.19; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.04-0.98; P = .047). The complementary full-cohort analysis included 347 women and 58 disease-free survival events. Pregnancy modeled as a time-dependent exposure was not associated with an increased event hazard (HR, 0.62; 95% CI, 0.29-1.33; P = .223). Pregnancy after breast cancer was not associated with worse disease-free survival in either analytical approach. The favorable matched estimate should not be interpreted as evidence that pregnancy prevents recurrence because residual healthy-mother selection and the limited number of events remain important considerations.

papers.abstract: This study aimed to introduce a first-cycle β-hCG response marker for predicting first-line single-agent chemoresistance in low-risk gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (GTN). This retrospective study included 299 patients. Patients were randomly assigned to a development cohort (n = 198) and internal validation cohort (n = 101). The primary exposure was the C2/C1 β-hCG ratio, defined as the serum β-hCG level before cycle 2 divided by the level before cycle 1. Restricted cubic spline and receiver operating characteristic analyses were used to derive the optimal threshold. Three models were evaluated: a FIGO-only model, a baseline clinical model, and a first-cycle dynamic model incorporating the C2/C1 ratio. First-line single-agent chemoresistance occurred in 45 patients in the development cohort and 23 in the internal validation cohort. The optimal C2/C1 β-hCG threshold was 0.38. Patients with a poor first-cycle response had higher chemoresistance rates than favorable responders in both the development cohort (43.8% vs. 8.5%) and internal validation cohort (44.7% vs. 9.5%). The dynamic model showed superior discrimination compared with the baseline clinical model, with AUCs of 0.867 in the development cohort and 0.844 in the internal validation cohort. Addition of the C2/C1 ratio improved calibration, reduced Brier scores, and yielded significant reclassification improvement. Poor responders required more cycles to β-hCG normalization, more total chemotherapy cycles, and more frequent second-line or multi-agent therapy. The first-cycle C2/C1 β-hCG ratio showed potential for predicting first-line single-agent chemoresistance in low-risk GTN. A threshold of 0.38 may help identify patients requiring closer monitoring, but requires prospective multicenter validation.

papers.abstract: Studies suggest that survival after a childhood central nervous system (CNS) tumor varies across social factors, but findings are inconsistent and largely based on older cohorts. We aimed to determine whether social factors were associated with childhood CNS tumor survival and explored how this association has evolved over time in three Nordic countries. This register-based cohort study included children aged 0-19 years diagnosed with a CNS tumor during 1993-2022 in Sweden, Denmark, and Finland (aged 0-15 years, 1993-2016 in Finland). Parental educational level was examined in all three countries. Additional individual-level (parental country of birth, employment status, cohabitation, and household disposable income) and area-based (education, income) social factors were studied in Sweden and Denmark. Using Cox regression models, we estimated adjusted hazard ratios (aHR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) to evaluate the association between social factors and 10-year all-cause mortality. Among 4703 children diagnosed with CNS tumors, social factors were not uniformly associated with mortality across the study period. Among children diagnosed 1993-2007, lower maternal and area-based educational levels were associated with higher mortality (comparing least vs. most educated groups: aHR, 95% CI maternal education: 1.30, 1.03-1.65; area-based education: 1.36, 0.99-1.88). Among children diagnosed 2008-2022, children with one Nordic and one non-Nordic parent had higher mortality than children with only Nordic parents (aHR: 1.54; 95% CI: 1.09-2.19). In conclusion, while education-related disparities seem to have diminished in recent years, emerging differences by parental country of birth warrant continued monitoring.

papers.abstract: During the past two decades, increasing evidence has indicated that sessile serrated lesions (SSLs) contribute to "interval" colon cancers. These cancers occur more frequently in women and develop predominantly in the proximal colon; however, our understanding of the risk factors contributing to the development and progression of proximal SSLs remains incomplete. We performed a cross-sectional study of 3746 consecutive patients who underwent high-definition endoscopy from 2011 to 2015 at John Dempsey Hospital. Proximal serrated lesions (SLs) were divided into high- and low-risk groups based on current recommendations. Multivariate logistic regression analysis was performed to determine independent risk factors for proximal SL occurrence, with a secondary analysis specific to high-risk SLs. 233 patients (6.2%) had at least one proximal SSL. Sixty-five (1.7%) showed histological evidence of high-risk SLs. Older age, non-Hispanic white, and colonoscopy indication were each independently associated with the presence of proximal SLs. Smoking history (odds ratio (OR) 1.4, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.13-1.61) and daily aspirin use (OR 0.5, 95% CI: 0.33-0.68) were also associated with the risk of proximal SLs. Upon secondary analyses, high-risk SLs were found to occur more frequently in women (OR 1.8, CI: 1.12-3.05) and smokers (OR 1.5, CI: 1.12-2.09). In conclusion, female gender and smoking represent a higher risk group for high-risk SLs in the proximal colon. Considering the higher prevalence of right-sided colorectal cancer (CRC) among women, these data add to the growing literature implicating proximal SLs in disease pathogenesis that may influence CRC screening guidelines.

papers.abstract: 73% of women dying from breast cancer (BC) come from low- or middle-income countries. These countries often do not have national mammography screening programmes. A less resource-demanding option is screening through clinical breast examination (CBE). As limited evidence exists for its effectiveness, two CBE trials have been conducted in India to assess efficacy with different designs and results. This study aims to model the natural history of BC and the performance of CBE using data from both trials to estimate the long-term effects of CBE and alternative screening scenarios. We used the well-established microsimulation model MISCAN-Fadia and utilized region-specific incidence, trial-specific inputs (such as screening interval, screening ages, attendance, and treatment regimens) to construct trial-specific models. We reported outcomes for both Trivandrum and Mumbai models with respectively 14 and 20 years follow-up time, as well as lifetime follow-up. The stage distribution in both trials was accurately reproduced by the models. Our models estimated BC mortality reductions between 5% and 6% for the Indian CBE trials, which were higher than reported by the CBE Trivandrum trial and lower than the Mumbai trial. When assuming 100% attendance with triennial screening between age 30-69 and a lifetime follow-up, model results showed a BC mortality reduction of 12%. Women in resource-limited countries may benefit from CBE screening, which given resources should not be seen as second-best. Screening with CBE in a broad age range of 30-69 can lead to reductions in BC mortality.

papers.abstract: Long-term female breast cancer survivors are at increased risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD), yet the biological mechanisms underlying this vulnerability remain poorly defined. Identifying non-invasive biomarkers capable of capturing early cardiovascular alterations in this population represents a relevant unmet clinical need. Twenty-four long-term female breast cancer survivors were enrolled and stratified according to cardiovascular disease history (CVD+, n = 12; CVD-, n = 12) and matched by age. A selected panel of 13 circulating microRNAs (miRNAs), together with adipokines and inflammatory cytokines, was analyzed in plasma samples. No significant differences were observed between groups in circulating adipokines or inflammatory markers. In contrast, miR-125b-5p and miR-210-3p were significantly downregulated in survivors with CVD compared with matched CVD- subjects. Correlation analyses revealed distinct, condition-specific association patterns between miRNA expression and cardiometabolic parameters. The reduced circulating expression of miR-125b-5p and miR-210-3p in long-term breast cancer survivors with cardiovascular disease suggests a potential involvement of these miRNAs in vascular homeostasis and hypoxia-related pathways. These findings support circulating miRNAs as promising exploratory biomarkers for cardiovascular risk stratification in cancer survivorship, warranting validation in larger prospective studies.

papers.abstract: Cardiometabolic disease and obesity are important factors when considering breast cancer risk and survivorship. We aimed to utilize a fully automated deep learning algorithm to evaluate CT-derived cardiometabolic biomarkers in patients with breast cancer. We applied fully automated deep learning algorithms to derive cardiometabolic markers from baseline computed tomography (CT) abdomen scans of females with breast cancer diagnosed between 2016 - 2018 at Johns Hopkins. Among 127 females (64.6% postmenopausal; 57.5% White and 26.8% Black race), BMI (body mass index) was positively correlated with CT-derived adipose tissue area and​ muscle area, and negatively correlated with liver intensity, but not associated with presence of aortic calcification. However, myosteatosis and menopausal status outperformed BMI as clinical markers of cardiometabolic health​ in breast cancer, as they were associated with both adiposity (especially visceral adiposity) and the presence of aortic calcification, with myosteatosis also being associated with liver steatosis. Artificial intelligence algorithms can feasibly and directly quantify body composition, liver fat, and abdominal aortic plaque, and be a tool in evaluating metabolic disease risk in patients with breast cancer.

papers.abstract: Natural killer (NK) cells are promising candidates for adoptive immunotherapy, but their ex vivo expansion is often accompanied by reduced cellular fitness and functional heterogeneity. Here, we identified that dasatinib, an FDA-approved tyrosine kinase inhibitor, could improve the expansion and antitumor function of NK cells. While dasatinib treatment from the start of culture impaired NK cell expansion, the introduction of dasatinib after the early expansion phase improved NK cell yields and viability without compromising NK cell purity. Transcriptomic analysis showed that dasatinib priming suppressed inflammatory signaling pathways and reduced the expression of apoptosis-related genes. Both transcriptomic and phenotypic analyzes further demonstrated downregulation of inhibitory signaling components, including SHP-1 and killer cell immunoglobulin-like receptor (KIR) family members. In line with these molecular changes, dasatinib-primed NK cells displayed enhanced cytotoxicity against tumor cells expressing high levels of MHC class I, consistent with modulation of MHC class I-related inhibitory signaling. Moreover, dasatinib priming improved the antitumor activity of anti-CD19 CAR-NK cells and enhanced cytotoxicity against MHC class I-expressing CD19+ tumor cells. Collectively, these findings identify dasatinib priming as a simple and clinically applicable strategy to improve the function and antitumor efficacy of expanded NK cells and CAR-NK cells.

papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint blockade has reshaped the treatment landscape of advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet durable responses remain limited to a subset of patients. Increasing evidence indicates that therapeutic resistance cannot be explained solely by T-cell exhaustion or PD-1/PD-L1 expression, but is actively shaped by an interconnected myeloid ecosystem. In HCC, tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), tumor-associated neutrophils (TANs), and myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) integrate signals from oncogenic pathways, chronic liver injury, fibrosis, metabolic stress, vascular remodeling, and therapy-induced damage. TAM subsets such as TREM2⁺, MARCO⁺, and CX3CR1⁺ macrophages promote CD8⁺ T-cell exclusion, suppress innate immune sensing, and form spatially protected tumor niches. TANs contribute to immune escape through immunosuppressive neutrophil states, neutrophil extracellular traps, CD73-adenosine signaling, and direct impairment of CD8⁺ T cells. MDSCs expand in response to radiofrequency ablation, chemotherapy resistance, fibrosis-associated inflammation, and immune checkpoint pressure, reinforcing PD-L1-, VEGF-A-, S100A9-, and TGF-β-related suppression. This review summarizes recent experimental evidence defining macrophage-neutrophil-MDSC crosstalk in HCC immune escape and immunotherapy resistance. We also discuss how other therapeutic pressures, including locoregional therapy and chemotherapy, can reshape the myeloid ecosystem and thereby influence subsequent immune control. Finally, we highlight myeloid-targeted strategies, biomarker development, etiology-informed stratification, and ecosystem-guided combinations aimed at improving immunotherapy outcomes in HCC.

papers.abstract: Lysine lactylation (Kla) is a post-translational modification implicated in tumor metabolic reprogramming, yet its functional significance in bladder cancer remains largely unexplored. Here, we identify lactylation of Lamin A in bladder cancer and elucidate its regulatory mechanisms in cisplatin resistance. Integrated lactylome and proteome profiling combined with mass spectrometry reveal that Lamin A is lactylated at K233 and K417, which are significantly elevated in bladder cancer tissues. Functional characterization demonstrates that lactylation of Lamin A suppresses tumor proliferation, inhibits migration, induces G1 cell cycle arrest, promotes apoptosis, and thus enhances cisplatin sensitivity, whereas lactylation-deficient mutants abrogate these effects, with K233 and K417 as the critical functional residues. Mechanistically, Lamin A delactylation enhances the binding between MRE11 and ATM, promotes the recruitment of MRE11 to DSB sites and activates the downstream CHK1/CHK2 signaling pathway, thereby promoting DNA repair and conferring cisplatin resistance. We further identify HDAC2 and KAT2A as the delactylase and lactyltransferase of Lamin A, respectively, with HDAC2 driving malignant phenotypes through K233 and K417 delactylation. Pharmacological inhibition of HDAC2 with entinostat effectively suppresses xenograft tumor growth in vivo in a Lamin A lactylation-dependent manner. Collectively, our findings define Lamin A lactylation as a tumor-suppressive modification and uncover the HDAC2/KAT2A-Lamin A axis as a critical factor of cisplatin response, suggesting that targeting this pathway may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for bladder cancer.

papers.abstract: Carboplatin improves pathological complete response (pCR) in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), but its effect on long-term survival remains uncertain. We conducted a strict randomized-contrast meta-analysis to assess the incremental effect of adding carboplatin to otherwise substantially comparable chemotherapy regimens. PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched from database inception. Phase II/III randomized controlled trials comparing carboplatin-containing versus carboplatin-free otherwise substantially comparable chemotherapy regimens in non-metastatic TNBC were included. Directly reported HRs for trial-defined disease-control endpoints and OS, and odds ratios (ORs) for pCR were pooled using random-effects models. Sensitivity analyses assessed the robustness of the disease-control and OS findings. Seven randomized contrasts (2,627 randomized participants) contributed disease-control evidence. Carboplatin significantly improved trial-defined disease control (HR 0.779, 95% CI 0.671-0.904; p = 0.001; I2 = 40.6%) and increased pCR rates (OR 2.038, 95% CI 1.653-2.512; p < 0.001; I2 = 29.9%). The OS estimate favored carboplatin but was compatible with no effect (HR 0.810, 95% CI 0.627-1.046; p = 0.107; I2 = 41.4%). The sensitivity analysis restricted to aligned EFS-type endpoints remained favorable (HR 0.793, 95% CI 0.656-0.960; p = 0.017; I2 = 31.4%). Carboplatin addition significantly improves pCR and trial-defined disease control in TNBC when evaluated in otherwise substantially comparable randomized chemotherapy contrasts. However, the strict evidence did not establish an OS benefit.

papers.abstract: Adjuvant cyclin-dependent kinase 4/6 inhibitors (CDK4/6i), including abemaciclib and ribociclib, have improved outcomes in patients with high-risk hormone receptor-positive (HR+)/HER2-negative early breast cancer. However, optimal treatment strategies following recurrence during or after adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibition remain undefined, as pivotal trials in advanced disease provide limited evidence for this emerging population. This narrative review critically examines available clinical and translational evidence regarding relapse after adjuvant CDK4/6i, including resistance mechanisms, endocrine sensitivity, biomarker-directed therapies, CDK4/6i rechallenge, chemotherapy, and antibody-drug conjugates. A pragmatic clinical framework is proposed according to the intervals from CDK4/6i discontinuation and endocrine therapy, while integrating disease characteristics, molecular alterations, and treatment feasibility. Three clinical scenarios are identified: recurrence during or within 12 months after CDK4/6i discontinuation; recurrence more than 12 months after CDK4/6i cessation but during or shortly after endocrine therapy; and late recurrence following completion of both treatments. These categories facilitate clinical assessment but do not represent validated biological definitions of resistance. Evidence supporting CDK4/6i rechallenge and treatments targeting PIK3CA, AKT1, PTEN, or ESR1 alterations is largely extrapolated from metastatic populations. Similarly, the optimal positioning of chemotherapy and antibody-drug conjugates following adjuvant CDK4/6i exposure remains uncertain. Isolated locoregional recurrence requires a distinct, potentially curative multidisciplinary approach. Longitudinal molecular profiling, including circulating tumor DNA and tissue-based multiomics, may improve understanding of resistance and disease evolution. No established therapeutic sequence exists for patients relapsing after adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibition. Treatment selection should integrate relapse timing, endocrine sensitivity, reassessed tumor phenotype, actionable biomarkers, clinical urgency, prior treatment exposure, and patient preferences. Dedicated prospective registries and randomized trials incorporating longitudinal molecular characterization are urgently needed to develop biologically informed treatment strategies.

papers.abstract: The ability to evaluate radiotherapy plans is a core clinical decision-making competency for trainees in radiation oncology (RO). This study aims to evaluate, through a prospective, multicenter randomized controlled trial (RCT), the effectiveness of scenario-based simulation teaching (SBST) using a typical defect case database compared to traditional lecture-based teaching in enhancing the treatment plan evaluation skills of RO trainees, and to analyze the impact of the pedagogical interventions on the trainees' cognitive psychological mechanisms. Forty RO trainees from three independent medical centers were enrolled and randomized into either the control (CON) or experimental (EXP) group. The CON group received traditional PowerPoint-based lectures focusing on standardized evaluation procedures and positive reference cases. The EXP group utilized the SBST model based on a typical defect case library, engaging in defect identification and feedback training within a high-fidelity plan evaluation environment. Primary endpoints included learning gains. Secondary endpoints encompassed cognitive load (NASA-TLX scale), multi-dimensional self-efficacy, and training satisfaction. Both groups exhibited significant post-training improvements and the EXP group achieved significantly higher normalized learning gains than the CON group (p < 0.0001), with results demonstrating high consistency across all participating centers. Regarding cognitive load, while no significant differences were observed between the two groups in mental demand or extraneous load (interference burden) during either training or post-test stages, the EXP group experienced a statistically significant reduction in post-test frustration (p < 0.05). Furthermore, the EXP group outperformed the CON group across all dimensions of self-efficacy and training satisfaction. This prospective multi-center RCT demonstrates that the SBST model, based on a typical defect case library, is superior and highly scalable for enhancing the clinical practice skills of RO trainees. By bolstering core competency and professional confidence, this study provides robust evidence for integrating this model into standardized and homogeneous radiation oncologist training programs.

papers.abstract: Microaxial flow pumps (mAFP) improve hemodynamics and outcomes in myocardial infarction-related cardiogenic shock (CS) but are associated with an increased risk of acute kidney injury (AKI) requiring renal replacement therapy (RRT). We aimed to determine the incidence and factors associated with RRT and evaluate its association with mortality in a real-world cohort of miscellaneous CS patients supported with mAFP. We conducted a retrospective multicentre registry including CS patients supported with mAFP across 11 European centres. The association between RRT and the primary outcome of 180-day all-cause mortality (with survival censored at heart transplantation or durable left ventricular assist device implantation) was assessed using a 1:1 propensity score-matched cohort. Factors associated with RRT were identified using multivariable logistic regression. Among 1043 patients, 972 were included, of whom 340 (35.0%) required RRT. RRT was associated with higher 180-day all-cause mortality both before (Kaplan-Meier estimates, 59.7% vs. 35.2%; HR 2.04, 95% CI 1.67-2.49; p < 0.01) and after propensity score matching (59.0% vs. 41.4%; HR 1.48, 95% CI 1.14-1.92; p < 0.01); restricted mean survival difference -25.5 days, 95% CI - 39.9 to -10.2. Factors associated with RRT included BMI ≥ 30 kg/m² (adjusted OR [aOR] 1.69; 95% CI 1.15-2.46), baseline serum creatinine (per 20 µmol/L increase: aOR 1.18; 95% CI 1.12-1.24), norepinephrine use (aOR 1.72; 95% CI 1.19-2.49), and lactate ≥4 mmol/L at implantation (aOR 1.56; 95% CI 1.11-2.20). In this large European registry of mAFP-supported CS, RRT was frequent and associated with increased 180-day mortality and greater shock severity.

papers.abstract: Cardiology consultations may be requested during preoperative anesthetic assessment before non-cardiac surgery. However, data regarding their impact on perioperative management are limited. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of preoperative cardiology consultations on perioperative patient management. We conducted a prospective, observational, single-center study in the Department of Anesthesiology and Critical Care at Angers University Hospital from September 1st, 2024, to August 31st, 2025. All patients referred for cardiology assessment after the anesthetic consultation were included. The primary endpoint was any change in perioperative management, including specific preoperative cardiac treatment, postponement or cancellation of surgery, and modification of anesthetic or surgical protocols. The secondary endpoint was to assess adherence of preoperative cardiac evaluation to current guideline recommendations. Among 9,621 preoperative anesthetic consultations, 138 (1%) patients were referred for cardiology assessment by the anesthesiologist and included in the study. 59 (43%) patients experienced a change in perioperative management. Of them, surgery was postponed in 52 (38%) patients, with a median delay of 81 [47-145] days, whereas only 6 patients underwent an invasive cardiac intervention (angioplasty, valvuloplasty, or electrical cardioversion). A previously unknown cardiac condition was identified in 19 (15%) patients. 111 (80%) cardiology referrals were consistent with current recommendations. In our study, preoperative cardiology consultations requested by an anesthesiologist were rare but frequently responsible for modification of perioperative management. These consultations often resulted in postponement of surgery, while only a small proportion of patients underwent an invasive cardiac intervention.

papers.abstract: Many patients present for surgery soon after concussion, when cerebral physiologic regulation may remain disturbed, and no evidence-based guideline or standardized consensus recommendations exist. We sought expert consensus for adults with recent concussion undergoing noncardiac extracranial surgery. We conducted a two-round modified Delphi study (November 2025-March 2026). Round 1 items, drafted from a systematic literature search, included case vignettes. Experts identified by bibliographic screening, directories, and nomination rated items on a five-point Likert scale; "do not know" responses were excluded from the denominator. Consensus was defined a priori as 75% agreement or greater, and strong consensus as 85% or greater. Thirty-five experts (33 anesthesiologists) from 17 countries completed both rounds; 13 of 16 Round 2 statements reached consensus. Agreement was unanimous for preoperative screening for concussion symptoms and neurologic red flags, and for avoidance of hypoxemia, abnormal carbon dioxide tension, sustained hypotension, and marked hypertension. Strong consensus supported generally deferring elective surgery until concussion symptoms resolve (97%), preoperative counseling (97%), structured follow-up (94%), and extended postoperative monitoring in higher-risk patients (91%). Consensus was not reached for regional anesthesia or monitored anesthesia care over general anesthesia (74%), electroencephalography-based depth of anesthesia monitoring (73%), or cautious long-acting neuraxial opioid use (69%). The panel did not define symptom resolution and established no symptom-independent waiting interval or concussion-specific numeric physiologic threshold. This anesthesiology-led consensus supports symptom-guided timing, physiologic stability, counseling, and structured follow-up; anesthetic technique, electroencephalographic monitoring, and neuraxial opioid use remain unresolved. The statements form an expert-informed framework, not an evidence-based practice guideline.

papers.abstract: Acute pain in the postoperative period and pre-existing cognitive impairment (CI) are both independently associated with increased postoperative adverse outcomes. Pre-existing cognitive impairment may interfere with the reporting, recognition, and treatment of pain in this population. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the impact of pre-existing cognitive impairment on pain and analgesic consumption after surgery in adults. MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Central, and Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews were searched for randomized controlled trials and cohort studies for adults undergoing non-cardiac, emergency, or elective surgery until April 9, 2026. Surgical patients with pre-existing cognitive impairment were compared to cognitively intact peers. The primary outcomes assessed were subjective ratings of pain and analgesic consumption postoperatively. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I and certainty of evidence was rated by GRADE. Meta-analysis used standard mean differences (SMDs) with 95% confidence intervals. Thirteen studies (37,918 patients) were included. Approximately one third (33%; 95% CI 0.25-0.41) of adult surgical patients screened positive for preoperative cognitive impairment. Subjective pain scores did not differ significantly between patients with and without cognitive impairment (Hedge's g: 0.11 (SD -0.15-0.36, I2 85.3%, T2 0.073). Patients with cognitive impairment had significantly less analgesic consumption than their cognitively intact counterparts (Cohen's d: 0.53 (0.29-0.76, I2 67.4%, T2 0.028). Despite comparable pain scores, those with cognitive impairment received significantly less postoperative analgesia, raising concern for systematic under-recognition and undertreatment of pain. Increased awareness of this discrepancy and the use of standardized analgesia protocols may improve postoperative outcomes. International Registry of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO:1117357).

papers.abstract: Our objectives were to evaluate the comparative clinical outcomes of cytoreductive surgery with or without hyperthermic intrathoracic chemotherapy (HITCH) for thymic epithelial tumors (TETs) with pleural dissemination and to assess the utility of a novel Pleural Tumor Index (PTI) as a practical prognostic tool to guide patient selection. This retrospective study evaluated patients with pleural-disseminated TETs who underwent surgery with or without HITCH. The HITCH protocol utilized a standardized sequential dual-agent hyperthermic perfusion (43 °C for 60 mins per session): doxorubicin (25 mg/m2) on postoperative day 1, followed by cisplatin (50 mg/m2) on postoperative day 2. The PTI was used to quantify pleural tumor burden. Propensity score matching was performed to balance baseline covariates. Perioperative and oncological outcomes were compared. Of 130 enrolled patients, 66 received surgery plus HITCH (Surg+HITCH) and 64 underwent surgery alone, yielding 44 propensity score-matched pairs. Surg+HITCH was associated with improved 3-year progression-free survival (87.3% vs. 48.6%; hazard ratio 0.28; 95% confidence interval 0.11-0.66; P = 0.013) and lower recurrence (9.09% vs. 36.3%). A PTI score >10 indicated a higher risk of tumor progression. Complication rates were slightly higher in the Surg+HITCH group (75.0% vs. 65.9%) but predominantly involved minor events without increasing intensive care unit stay or mortality. Surg+HITCH safely improves long-term tumor control in patients with pleural-disseminated TETs. The PTI serves as a practical tool for risk stratification to guide patient selection. Further prospective studies are required to validate our findings.

papers.abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is a highly prevalent and aggressive malignancy often characterized by lymph node metastasis, a key contributor to its poor prognosis. Although NSUN2 functions as an oncogene in LUAD through m5C-dependent mechanisms, its specific role in regulating malignant progression remains elusive. This study aimed to investigate the role and mechanism of NSUN2 in regulating this progress. Cell viability and proliferation of A549 and PC9 cells were detect by cell-counting kit-8 and 5-ethynyl-2'-deoxyuridine (EdU) staining. Migration and invasion were evaluated by Transwell and wound-healing assays. Flow cytometry was performed to detect apoptosis, whereas Western blot was performed to evaluate the levels of proteins related to epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and lymphangiogenesis (Snail, vimentin, MMP2, MMP9, vascular endothelial growth factor C [VEGF-C] and E-cadherin). A LUAD xenograft model was constructed using BALB/c nude mice. The underlying mechanism was investigated by methylated RNA immunoprecipitation (MeRIP), RIP, RNA pull-down, and the like. NSUN2 expression was upregulated in LUAD tumor tissues and cell lines. In nude mice, NSUN2 knockdown inhibited A549 and PC9 cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, as well as xenograft tumor growth and VEGF-C expression. Mechanically, NSUN2 knockdown reduced Notch1 mRNA stability by decreasing its m5C modification. Overexpression of Notch1 reversed these inhibitory effects both in vitro and in vivo. Collectively, the study demonstrated that NSUN2 promoted LUAD progression through m5C-dependent Notch1 stability. These findings highlight the NSUN2-Notch1 m5C-dependent regulatory axis as a promising target for LUAD.

papers.abstract: Abstract Background Differentiating benign sclerosing angiomatoid nodular transformation (SANT) from solitary mass-forming primary splenic lymphoma (PSL) remains challenging because both can present as solitary splenic masses with overlapping imaging features. This study evaluated quantitative clinicopathologic and imaging features that may help distinguish these entities. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 11 patients with histologically confirmed SANT and 11 patients with solitary mass-forming PSL, selected from an institutional cohort of 100 consecutive PSL cases that presented as a solitary splenic mass. Demographic, radiologic, and pathologic variables were evaluated. Receiver operating characteristic analysis was used to evaluate the diagnostic performance of selected individual preoperative variables. Results Patients with solitary mass-forming PSL were significantly older than those with SANT (mean 53.3 vs. 37.9 years; p = 0.038) and exhibited substantially higher Ki-67 proliferation indices (63.3% vs. 4.4%; p = 0.003). Although focal lesion size did not differ significantly between the groups, whole-spleen burden was a major discriminator: maximal spleen diameter (18.4 vs. 12.0 cm; p = 0.015) and weight (1250 vs. 214 g; p = 0.036) were markedly higher in lymphoma. Spleen size alone achieved an area under the curve of 0.867, with a 16 cm threshold yielding 62.5% sensitivity and 100% specificity. Conclusions Solitary mass-forming PSL is characterized by whole-organ diffuse enlargement rather than focal lesion size, distinguishing it from localized SANT. Global splenic burden may provide an adjunctive imaging parameter for distinguishing solitary mass-forming PSL from SANT and may complement other clinical, imaging, and tissue-based assessments.

papers.abstract: Abstract Purpose Adjuvant chemotherapy (AC) improves survival in patients with resected stage II–III non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC); however, its benefits may not be universal. We aimed to identify subgroups in which the benefit of AC may be limited. Methods In this multicenter study, we retrospectively analyzed 1,307 patients with pathological stage II–III NSCLC who underwent complete resection (R0) between 2010 and 2022. Patients were stratified according to the presence of lymphatic (Ly), vascular (V), or pleural (pl) invasion. Overall survival (OS) and cumulative incidence of recurrence (CIR) were compared between the AC and non-AC groups using multivariate Cox regression and Fine–Gray competing-risk models. Results Overall, 775 patients did not receive AC, and 532 did. In the subgroup without Ly, V, or pl invasion (low-risk group), AC did not significantly improve OS (5-year OS: 79.3% vs. 74.3%, P = 0.66) or CIR (5-year CIR: 28.9% vs. 27.6%, P = 0.79). In patients with Ly, V, or pl invasion (high-risk group), AC was associated with better OS (5-year OS: 81.2% vs. 51.2%, P < 0.01) and lower CIR (5-year CIR: 49.9% vs. 52.1%, P = 0.04). Among patients with pathological node-positive disease (pN+), an OS benefit was observed only in the high-risk group. Conclusions In completely resected stage II–III NSCLC, the absence of Ly, V, and pl invasion identified a low-risk subgroup in which the survival benefit of AC appeared limited, particularly in pN0 disease. Pathological invasion status may help identify patients for whom the benefit of AC warrants further evaluation.

papers.abstract: In the phase III Opti-TROP-Lung06 trial, patients with newly diagnosed PD-L1-negative, advanced nonsquamous non-small cell lung cancer without targetable alterations who received the TROP-2-directed antibody-drug conjugate sacituzumab tirumotecan and the PD-1 inhibitor pembrolizumab experienced a median progression-free survival (PFS) of 15 months. In comparison, those patients who received standard chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab experienced a median PFS of 5.7 months.
