papers.abstract: Objective Critically ill patients with documented radiotherapy-related records represent a population in whom early short-term mortality assessment may be clinically relevant. We aimed to develop and validate an interpretable machine-learning model for predicting 28-day mortality in patients who remained observable through the first 24 h after ICU admission. Methods We included patients from MIMIC-IV for model training (n=908), the MIMIC-III CareVue subset v1.4 for temporal testing (n=499), and the eICU/local cohorts for external validation (n=118). Eligibility was determined solely by radiotherapy-related diagnosis or procedure records, which were not used as model predictors. Model predictors were derived primarily from information recorded during the first 24 h after ICU admission. Missing data were handled using multiple imputation. LASSO regression was used for feature selection in the training cohort. Seven machine-learning models were compared based on their discrimination, and the selected model was further evaluated using calibration, decision-curve analysis, and SHAP interpretation. A sensitivity analysis excluding sepsis and acute kidney injury was performed. Results The 28-day mortality rates were 11.56% (105/908), 11.62% (58/499), and 12.71% (15/118) in the training, temporal testing, and external validation cohorts, respectively. LASSO selected chloride, SOFA score, RDW, respiratory rate, sepsis, and acute kidney injury. In the temporal testing cohort, random forest achieved the highest observed AUC (0.868; 95% CI, 0.815-0.917) and showed greater discrimination than SOFA-based benchmarks, six-variable logistic regression, and ANN in paired comparisons. In the external validation cohort, random forest showed an AUC of 0.785 (95% CI, 0.650-0.909). After exclusion of sepsis and acute kidney injury, the observed AUC decreased to 0.843 in temporal testing and 0.713 in external validation; the paired confidence intervals for both AUC differences included zero. Conclusion A six-variable random forest model showed useful discrimination for 28-day mortality among ICU patients identified through radiotherapy-related records and maintained moderate discrimination in external validation. SHAP analysis enhanced model interpretability by illustrating the contribution of routinely available general ICU variables. Radiotherapy-related records served solely to define the study population; this study did not evaluate radiotherapy exposure or radiotherapy-specific mechanisms. These findings support further evaluation of the model for prognostic risk stratification in larger prospective cohorts.

papers.abstract: Objective This study aimed to systematically evaluate the effects of perioperative music-based interventions on psychological and physiological outcomes in patients undergoing breast cancer surgery. Methods CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, SinoMed, PubMed, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published up to October 2025. Two reviewers independently screened the studies, extracted data, and assessed methodological quality using the Cochrane risk-of-bias tool (RoB 1.0). A meta-analysis was conducted using RevMan 5.4 software. Effect sizes were expressed as mean differences (MD) or standardized mean differences (SMD) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Random-effects models were used when substantial heterogeneity was present, and sensitivity and subgroup analyses were conducted to explore robustness and potential sources of heterogeneity. Results A total of 18 RCTs involving 1,728 patients were included. The results showed that music-based interventions significantly improved postoperative anxiety (SMD = 0.99, 95% CI: 0.48–1.49, I ² = 91%, p = 0.0001), depression (SMD = 0.66, 95% CI: 0.44–0.88, I ² = 0%, p < 0.00001), and pain (SMD = 0.64, 95% CI: 0.31–0.97, I ² = 65%, P = 0.0001). In addition, music-based interventions significantly reduced systolic blood pressure (MD = 14.17, 95% CI: 5.66–22.67, I ² = 56%, P = 0.001), diastolic blood pressure (MD = 7.14, 95% CI: 0.48–13.79, I ² = 84%, p = 0.04), and heart rate (MD = 4.75, 95% CI: 1.02–8.48, I ² = 77%, P = 0.01). Subgroup analyses revealed that the effects on psychological and physiological outcomes differed by intervention timing and music playback mode. Conclusion Perioperative music-based interventions appear to be an effective, safe, and low-cost non-pharmacological approach for alleviating psychological distress, reducing pain, and stabilizing certain physiological stress indicators in patients undergoing breast cancer surgery. Further high-quality studies are needed to optimize intervention protocols and facilitate the standardized clinical application of music-based interventions in breast cancer rehabilitation. Systematic review registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251235397 , identifier CRD420251235397.

papers.abstract: Precision oncology based on the identification of actionable genomic alterations (AGAs) has been transformative in the care of solid tumors, yet optimal treatment selection is often hindered by tissue exhaustion and slow turnaround times. Artificial intelligence (AI) addresses these barriers by predicting AGAs directly from routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained slides. Recent landmark studies, including the prospective EAGLE and ANNAR trials, have demonstrated that deep learning models can identify alterations such as EGFR in non-small cell lung cancer and FGFR in urothelial cancer across diverse global cohorts. By providing near-instant, non-destructive results, AI-based prediction can triage patients for molecular testing or clinical trials at the time of initial diagnosis. This perspective evaluates the maturing evidence base and outlines a pragmatic pathway for integrating these tools into clinical practice. Ultimately, these models offer the opportunity to extract critical molecular information from slides generated in every laboratory worldwide and to significantly improve timely access to the rapidly evolving therapeutic landscape of solid tumors.

papers.abstract: Spatial proteomics enables high-resolution mapping of protein expression within the tumor microenvironment, but its routine clinical application remains limited by cost, technical complexity and restricted tissue coverage. Here we present Hist2Prot, a deep learning framework that generates single-cell spatial proteomic profiles from routine hematoxylin and eosin histology. Trained on approximately 51 million paired cells from a same-section G4X spatial proteomics dataset, Hist2Prot was evaluated in internal test cohorts, independent same-platform G4X cohorts and external cross-platform datasets comprising approximately 72 million additional cells, showing concordance with measured protein profiles and outperforming established baselines. Hist2Prot-derived virtual proteins preserved immune, stromal and tumor cell phenotypes and recapitulated clinically relevant tumor microenvironment organization. Across seven independent patient cohorts comprising 1,774 patients, virtual spatial proteomics improved molecular biomarker, prognostic and immunotherapy response prediction beyond hematoxylin and eosin morphology alone. Hist2Prot enables scalable single-cell computational spatial proteomics from routine histology for precision oncology.

papers.abstract: Risk reducing decisions impact previvors' identity, family experiences, and relationships. These decisions are especially challenging for non-BRCA previvors, who face vague guidelines and limited evidence. This qualitative study explored non-BRCA previvors' attitudes toward family planning, relationships, and the burden of previvor status. Previvors with non-BRCA mutations (Lynch-related, PALB2, RAD51C, BRIP1, CHEK2) were recruited from an urban gynecologic oncology clinic. We conducted semi-structured telephone interviews which were transcribed verbatim. Two investigators independently coded a subset of interviews, resolved discrepancies with a moderator blinded to study background, and then refined the codebook and applied across all transcripts to identify themes. Twenty-one previvors completed interviews (median age 39). Three overarching themes emerged: impact of previvor status on mental health, on personal identity, and impact of medical experience on decision making. Those considering future fertility worried about assisted reproductive technology (ART) cost and time pressure from risk reduction timelines; those not pursuing fertility worried about early menopause and mutation transmission to children. Previvor status impacted romantic relationships differently, with some describing strains caused by altered family planning and cancer prevention timelines, while others feeling no impact. Previvors emphasized the physician-patient relationship and shared decision-making. Many expressed frustrations regarding access to reliable data amid unclear guidelines. The lower penetrance of the non-BRCA did not lessen the psychosocial burden of previvor status in our cohort. Family planning, relationships, and previvor burden are central concerns for previvors. Ambiguity surrounding non-BRCA variants emerged as an independent source of distress shaping daily lives. Physicians can better partner with previvors by acknowledging these challenges to align medical and personal goals.

papers.abstract: Ribociclib plus letrozole demonstrated meaningful activity in recurrent low-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (LGSOC) in the phase II GOG-3026 trial. However, biomarkers associated with CDK4/6 inhibitor response remain undefined. We conducted an exploratory translational analysis to identify molecular and immune biomarkers associated with clinical outcomes. Archival FFPE tumors from 24 GOG-3026 patients were analyzed. Immunohistochemistry assessed ER, PR, p16, phosphorylated RB (pRB), and Ki-67. Whole-exome sequencing (n = 14) and RNA sequencing (n = 12) evaluated genomic alterations and immune transcriptional profiles. Associations between biomarkers and objective response rate (ORR), clinical benefit rate (CBR), progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival were evaluated using 2-sided tests at a 5% significance level, without multiple testing adjustment. Among 24 patients, ORR was 37.5% and CBR was 87.5%. Lower Ki-67 expression was significantly associated with CBR (r = -0.437, p = 0.0326). Higher p16 expression showed a trend toward shorter PFS (Cox proportional hazard regression: HR 2.8, 95% CI 0.96-9.20; Monte Carlo permutation log-rank test: p = 0.0633). ER, PR, pRB expression and MAPK pathway alterations were not associated with response or survival. The most common genomic alterations involved BRAF, KRAS, NRAS and FANCD2. RNA sequencing identified three immune phenotypes: immune-hot, intermediate, and immune-cold. No partial responders had an immune-hot phenotype, while four of five partial responders clustered in the intermediate group. Lower Ki-67 expression may predict clinical benefit from ribociclib plus letrozole, while higher p16 expression may be associated with shorter PFS. Distinct immune phenotypes may also influence response, supporting prospective validation of proliferation-, cell-cycle-, and immune-based biomarkers to refine patient selection for CDK4/6-directed therapy in LGSOC.

papers.abstract: T cell therapies with chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells or T cell receptor (TCR) transgenic (tg) T cells are a promising approach in the treatment of solid malignancies but are limited by T cell exhaustion caused by chronic antigen stimulation. Clusterin (CLU) is a stress-associated molecular chaperone with cytoprotective functions in normal and malignant cells, but its role in therapeutic T cells is unclear. Here, we found that CLU expression is reduced in exhausted tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes and decreases after prolonged stimulation of Ewing sarcoma (EwS)-directed TCR-transgenic T cells and GD2 CAR-T cells. To test whether reconstituting CLU affects T cell fitness, we engineered CHM1/HLA-A*02:01-directed ChoTCR-T cells and GD2 CAR-T cells to overexpress CLU. In ChoTCR-T cells, CLU overexpression reduced exhaustion- and apoptosis-associated features after repetitive tumor stimulation while preserving cytotoxicity. CLU-engineered ChoTCR-T cells showed improved infiltration of EwS spheroids, and moderately improved antitumor activity in a metastatic EwS model. Supportive experiments in a GD2/Nalm6 chronic-stimulation model indicated preserved CAR-T cell function after repetitive antigen exposure. Mechanistically, proteomics together with direct measurements of global translation and stress-response activation support a model in which CLU reduces proteostasis-linked translational stress during chronic stimulation. These findings identify CLU overexpression as a promising strategy to attenuate chronic-stimulation-associated dysfunction in tumor-directed T cells, as shown in two therapeutic T cell models of cancer in the young.

papers.abstract: Time-resolved, network-wide consequences of cancer metabolic reprogramming remain poorly understood. We built multi-omics-constrained, near-genome-scale kinetic ensembles for isogenic BRCA1 wild-type and BRCA1-mutant ovarian cancer cells. Covering over 2,100 reactions, the ensembles enabled uncertainty-quantified simulations of nutrient, metabolite, and enzyme perturbations. Metabolic control analysis identified 28 enzyme-mediated vulnerabilities; 24 are linked to experimental or approved DrugBank compounds, whereas four lack documented drug associations. Independent DepMap data supported a subset of these candidates. All 28 emerged directly from the mechanistic model structure and multi-omics constraints, with no calibration to known drug targets or cancer-dependency data. Simulations of thymidylate synthase, hexokinase, and triokinase inhibition predicted target- and physiology-specific changes in pathway use, energy metabolism, and a shared ceramide-linked stress response. Mapping predicted enzyme-activity shifts to BRCA1-associated transcription factors suggested regulatory routes underlying differences between the two states. These ensembles provide a reusable framework for time-resolved, mechanistic hypothesis generation across cancers and other diseases. A record of this paper's transparent peer review process is included in the supplemental information.

papers.abstract: Extraembryonic tissues and many cancers share unusual DNA methylation landscapes, but how these states arise remains unclear. Here, we use GATA6- and CDX2-driven reprogramming of mouse embryonic stem cells to track genome-wide epigenetic remodeling during acquisition of extraembryonic cell fates. Despite activating distinct transcriptional programs from non-overlapping genomic targets, both transcription factors trigger rapid and genomically synchronized convergence to cancer-like DNA methylation patterns, including simultaneous global DNA methylation loss and de novo methylation of Polycomb-regulated CpG islands. We find that this wave of DNA methylation reprogramming co-occurs with global H3K27me3 redistribution alongside promoter H3K4 methylation loss. Experimental models of cellular senescence, as well as human aging and cancer cohorts, reveal related but progressively more extensive disruption of these same chromatin boundaries. Together, these data define a tractable system for studying coordinated genome-wide transitions between canonical and non-canonical epigenomic states.

papers.abstract: This study combines RNA sequencing data from 1,824 tumors across major lung cancer types to examine how tumor gene expression patterns relate to histologic diagnoses. The resulting reference landscape identifies nine transcriptional clusters, including a neuroendocrine-like adenocarcinoma group and regions with mixed histology. The clusters also show associations with clinical features, genetic alterations, immune characteristics, and survival. An interactive Oncoscape resource allows researchers to explore the integrated data and compare patient tumors with patient-derived xenograft models.

papers.abstract: Optimal integration of induction chemoimmunotherapy with definitive chemoradiotherapy (CRT) and maintenance immunotherapy for unresectable stage III NSCLC remains undefined. This multicenter retrospective study included 321 patients who received induction chemoimmunotherapy followed by CRT with or without maintenance immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). Landmark survival from radiotherapy completion was used to avoid guarantee-time bias. Patients receiving 1-2 induction cycles showed numerically longer median PFS (28.0 months) than those with 3-4 (24.6) or >4 cycles (14.2; log-rank p = 0.179), but this trend was confounded by higher concurrent CRT rates in the 1-2 cycle group (74.5%vs. 47.1% vs. 33.7%). After propensity-score matching, the response-related survival advantage was attenuated (HR for PFS 0.70, p = 0.079). In matched analyses, maintenance ICI was associated with improved PFS (25.2 vs. 8.9 months; HR 0.47) and OS (NR vs. 22.0 months; HR 0.24) (both p 9 maintenance cycles yielded further PFS (HR 0.23) and OS (HR 0.17) benefits. In this real-world cohort, induction cycle number did not significantly affect survival; the apparent advantage of 1-2 cycles was likely confounded. Early radiographic response was not an independent predictor after matching. Maintenance ICI was associated with improved outcomes, and >9 cycles showed additional benefit, though with potential bias. These findings provide hypotheses for prospective trial design.

papers.abstract: Breast cancer (BC) is the most commonly diagnosed cancer among women and a leading cause of cancer mortality worldwide. Understanding and addressing the barriers women face in accessing BC care is crucial for improving clinical outcomes and public health. This paper describes and discusses the findings from a systematic literature review (SLR) of the barriers that women worldwide face in accessing mammography screening and diagnosis, which may lead to delays in BC treatment. We also aimed to estimate the number of women worldwide affected by delayed or absent. We also aimed to estimate the number of women affected by delayed or absent access to medical services. The systematic literature review included a comprehensive search in bibliographic databases and grey literature. A total of 20,434 citations were identified, with 2,611 citations eligible for full-text examination, which resulted in 256 extracted sources fulfilling the inclusion criteria. We focused on quantitative data on the number of patients whose access to BC-related medical services was hindered by such barriers. The review identified education, age, and geographic region as important factors influencing barriers to mammography. Educational level, residential location, and travel time showed the strongest associations with delay in BC diagnosis. Socio-demographic characteristics also had an impact on the stage of cancer at diagnosis. An estimated 869.8 million women are aged 50-75 years worldwide. Of these, approximately 679.7 million women (78%) do not receive mammography because either their country has no established mammography program (557.7 million) or because existing programs have low uptake rates for various reasons (122.1 million). Of the 2.3 million new BC cases annually worldwide, approximately 796,000 women may experience delay in diagnosis and/or treatment initiation. In an exploratory, scenario-based approximation, nearly 127,000 deaths each year could be associated with delay in diagnosis and/or treatment initiation due to more advanced disease presentation and postponed interventions. These findings highlight the challenges women face in accessing mammography programs and the large number of women living in regions without mammography coverage (e.g., due to socioeconomic status or distance to a mammography center). They underscore the urgent need for the WHO Global Breast Cancer Initiative, which aims to establish early detection programs to promote earlier diagnosis and reduce BC mortality, especially in low- and middle-income countries.

papers.abstract: Gallbladder cancer (GBC) is an aggressive malignancy with limited treatment options for advanced disease. Bortezomib (BTZ) has shown activity against biliary tract cancers, but acquired resistance severely undermines its clinical benefit. To elucidate the underlying mechanisms and identify strategies to reverse resistance, we established a BTZ-resistant GBC-SD cell line. Resistant cells overexpressed plasma membrane-localized P-glycoprotein (P-gp), exhibited efflux of multiple substrates, and acquired cross-resistance to other proteasome inhibitors, confirming multidrug resistance (MDR). Pharmacological inhibition with tariquidar or genetic ablation of ABCB1 reversed MDR in vitro and suppressed tumor growth in xenograft models. Whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatics revealed ABCB1 amplification within a putative circular amplicon, indicative of extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA), and identified single-nucleotide polymorphisms associated with resistance. Proximity labeling coupled with mass spectrometry further identified histone H1 and HNRNPU as key regulators of the amplicon. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that ecDNA-mediated ABCB1 amplification drives P-gp overexpression and MDR in GBC, and that this resistance can be effectively reversed by targeting P-gp or the amplicon complex. This work provides a mechanistic foundation for developing therapeutic strategies to overcome ecDNA-driven drug resistance in GBC and other refractory malignancies.

papers.abstract: Fusobacterium nucleatum has been linked to chemoresistance and immune evasion in colorectal cancer (CRC), but therapeutic strategies targeting this bacterium remain limited. In this multicenter, single-arm, phase 2 trial (NCT06356597), 33 patients with Fusobacterium nucleatum-positive, microsatellite-stable metastatic CRC received the combination treatment of tislelizumab, fruquintinib, and the antimicrobial metronidazole. The primary endpoint was met, with a median progression-free survival of 6.0 months. The objective response rate and disease control rate were 19.4% and 83.9%, respectively. Grade 3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 30.3% of patients, with no grade 4 or 5 events. Metagenomic analysis showed that metronidazole reduced Fusobacterium nucleatum abundance. Exploratory analyses associated clinical benefit with enrichment of Lactobacillus species and nonresponse with Enterococcus. Fecal microbiota transplantation from responders sensitized germ-free mice to the treatment, which enhanced cytotoxic CD8+ T cell differentiation and reduced terminal exhaustion. These findings support further evaluation of this combination in Fusobacterium nucleatum-positive metastatic CRC.

papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) exhibits a highly complex tumor microenvironment enriched with both inflammatory and immunosuppressive factors. Interleukin-18 (IL-18), a cytokine of the IL-1 family, is elevated in PDAC and correlates with poor patient outcomes. However, the functional role of IL-18 in PDAC progression and immune regulation remains poorly defined. We generated genetically engineered mouse models with IL-18 depletion in the context of spontaneous PDAC development. Single-cell RNA-sequencing and functional assays were used to analyze PDAC progression, macrophage phenotypes, and cancer cell-macrophage interactions. Mechanistic studies were performed to determine the effects of IL-18 on STAT1 signaling and CD47 expression. The role of IL-18 in therapeutic response was evaluated using KRAS inhibitor (KRASi) treatment models. Elevated IL-18 expression correlated with poor patient survival. Genetic depletion of IL-18 significantly suppressed spontaneous PDAC progression and prolonged survival in mice. Mechanistically, IL-18 promoted cancer cell survival by activating STAT1-dependent CD47 expression, thereby impairing macrophage-mediated phagocytosis of cancer cells. In addition, IL-18 depletion reshaped the tumor immune microenvironment by enriching macrophage populations with enhanced antigen-presenting and phagocytic phenotypes characterized by increased MHCII and CD11c expression. Notably, KRAS inhibitor treatment further increased IL-18 expression in PDAC cells, whereas IL-18 depletion enhanced macrophage-mediated clearance of KRASi-treated cancer cells and improved therapeutic efficacy. IL-18 promotes pancreatic cancer progression by enabling cancer cell survival and immune evasion through macrophage reprogramming. Targeting IL-18 may represent a therapeutic strategy to enhance macrophage-mediated anti-tumor immunity and improve responses to KRAS inhibitor therapies in PDAC.

papers.abstract: Aromatase inhibitors (AIs) have transformed the treatment of hormone receptor-positive breast cancer by suppressing estrogen biosynthesis. However, aromatase and estrogen signaling have also been implicated in several malignancies traditionally classified as non-hormone-dependent, where their effects on tumor progression, metabolism, and antitumor immunity appear to depend on tumor type, receptor context, and the tumor microenvironment. This emerging evidence has generated increasing interest in repurposing AIs beyond their conventional endocrine indications. In this review, we summarize the molecular mechanisms linking aromatase and estrogen signaling to oncogenic pathways, tumor metabolism, and modulation of the tumor microenvironment in non-hormone-dependent malignancies. We further discuss preclinical studies demonstrating that AIs not only inhibit intratumoral estrogen production but also enhance the efficacy of chemotherapy and immune checkpoint inhibitors by suppressing pro-survival signaling, reducing PD-L1 expression, reshaping lipid metabolism, and restoring antitumor immune responses. Finally, we critically examine the currently available clinical studies, highlighting both the encouraging biological rationale and the limitations of existing early-phase trials. Overall, aromatase can be considered a broad regulator of cancer biology. Addressing three major challenges - accurate patient stratification, precise identification of predictive biomarkers and design of prospective clinical trials -will be essential to realize the translational potential of AIs and determine whether they can enhance current anticancer treatments.

papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Actinic keratosis (AK) is the most common precancerous cutaneous lesion and may progress through squamous cell carcinoma in situ (SCCIS) to cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC). The PI3K–mTOR pathway is hyperactivated across this spectrum, yet no approved therapy targets it. We evaluated topical bimiralisib (PQR309), a pan-class I PI3K inhibitor with activity against mTOR, and developed a topical bimiralisib gel. Methods: K14-Fyn-Y528F transgenic mice received topical bimiralisib 1% (w/w) or a vehicle daily for 4 weeks, or 50 mg kg−1 orally. Human cSCC explants were incubated with bimiralisib 0.1–10 µmol L−1, and UV-B-irradiated SKH-1 mice received topical bimiralisib 3% (w/w), a vehicle or no treatment, with imiquimod as a comparator. Two of fourteen formulations underwent in vitro release and permeation testing as well as in vivo porcine penetration testing. Results: Topical bimiralisib reduced the lesion area by >99% at 4 weeks, restoring unremarkable epidermis and normalising PI3K–mTOR, MAPK and Src-family signalling without erythema or crusting, while oral dosing was inactive (mean reduction 35%; p ≥ 0.2). Phospho-Akt fell in a concentration-dependent manner in human explants, and lead gels delivered epidermal concentrations at or above the IC90 required for pathway inhibition. In the UV-B-irradiated SKH-1 model, topical bimiralisib prevented cSCC occurrence and Ki-67 labelling but did not reduce atypia in AKs or SCCIS. Conclusions: Activity is governed by epidermal drug exposure rather than intrinsic potency, supporting topical dual PI3K–mTOR inhibition as a non-inflammatory field-directed strategy for AK.

papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) models for solid renal mass characterization show promising discrimination in multicenter and some prospective test sets, yet little published evidence supports their routine clinical use. We examine four translation gaps. Independent, representative validation remains limited, and most studies use resected, pathologically confirmed masses, underrepresenting small indeterminate lesions managed by biopsy or surveillance. Recent multicenter models, including RenalCLIP and MPANet, broadened tasks and external testing but remain retrospective. Four retrospective reader experiments suggest that AI assistance can improve readers’ accuracy or consistency, but no study identified measured effects on management or patient outcomes. Regulatory evidence is limited: one renal tool reported by its manufacturer as certified under the European Union Medical Device Regulation rests on a single-center retrospective reader study of detection and reporting, and no characterization device was identified in the U.S. Food and Drug Administration AI-enabled device list. The 2026 European Association of Urology guidelines discuss AI as an emerging technology without a graded recommendation. Cost, information technology integration, trust, and interpretability further restrict adoption. We propose a roadmap built around one intended use, the small indeterminate solid mass considered for biopsy or surveillance, with prespecified thresholds, target-specific reference standards, and paired management and safety endpoints.

papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Breast surgery currently ranks among the most frequently performed surgical procedures globally, reflecting advances in medicine. The most important developments among minimally invasive surgeries are sentinel node biopsy techniques in clinically node-negative patients and new localization procedures used for impalpable breast tumors. Methods: In this study, we used SCOUT® technology for localizing breast tumors and/or metastatic axillary nodes in conjunction with sentinel node detection using SPIO nanoparticles (Magtrace®) and a magnetic probe (Sentimag®). Results: A total of 109 seeds were placed in 96 patients, the majority of whom underwent breast-conserving surgery. The SCOUT® radar localization system successfully localized all impalpable breast tumors. Tumor-free surgical margins were found in 89 patients (92.7%) upon postoperative histology assessment. Additional re-excision was needed for 7 patients (7.3%). Sentinel lymph nodes (SLNs) were detectable in all patients. The mean number of nodes removed per patient was 3.3 (SD = 1.76 nodes; median = 3; IQR = 2–3). Conclusions: Our experience with dual-probe technique demonstrates the viability of combined radar and magnetic guidance in early breast cancer surgery, especially in settings without access to nuclear medicine.

papers.abstract: Malignant hyperthermia (MH) is a rare pharmacogenetic condition with substantial morbidity and mortality. The current gold standard for diagnosis, caffeine-halothane contracture testing (CHCT), is invasive, costly, and available only at a single centre in Canada. Genetic testing offers a less invasive alternative, but access remains inconsistent across Canadian provinces. We sought to evaluate the cost-consequences and diagnostic wait times of a genetics-first vs biopsy-first strategy for MH susceptibility. We conducted a retrospective cost-consequence analysis of 1,208 patients referred to the Canadian Malignant Hyperthermia Investigation Unit (2015-2024) with a personal or family history suggestive of MH, and their first-degree relatives. We compared the direct, indirect, and societal costs of the Ontario genetics-first approach with those of a hypothetical biopsy-first approach used in other provinces. We analyzed diagnostic timelines using Kaplan-Meier survival analyses. In the genetics-first strategy, 7.2% of probands (88/1,208) had a diagnostic variant and did not require biopsy for contracture testing, resulting in modest societal cost reduction for probands compared with the biopsy-first strategy (CAD 23.5M vs CAD 24.3M, respectively; CAD 700 saved per proband tested). The costs of cascade testing of their first-degree relatives were three-fold lower for the genetics-first strategy (CAD 3.6M vs CAD 11.3M). The median [interquartile range] time to diagnosis was 2 [1-5] months for patients with diagnostic variants, compared with 39 [22-51] months for those requiring biopsy (log-rank P < 0.001). Compared with a hypothetical biopsy-first approach, offering genetics testing as initial step to all individuals with clinical suspicion of MH susceptibility did not increase societal costs, and resulted in substantial cost savings for cascade testing of their relatives, markedly shortening time to diagnosis for individuals who harbour a diagnostic variant.

papers.abstract: Intravenous lipid emulsion (ILE) is the recommended first-line treatment for local anesthetic systemic toxicity (LAST), particularly when cardiovascular compromise occurs. However, uncertainty persists regarding the optimal lipid formulation, specifically the comparative efficacy of ILEs containing 100% long-chain triglycerides (LCT) versus ILEs containing a 50/50 mixture of medium- and long-chain triglycerides (MCT/LCT), as well as ILEs with a 20% versus 30% lipid concentration. The primary aim of this narrative review was to compare the efficacy of 100% LCT-containing ILEs versus 50% MCT/LCT-containing ILEs by analyzing their respective mechanisms of action in experimental models of local anesthetic-induced cardiovascular toxicity, whereas the secondary objective was to compare ILEs with a 20% versus a 30% lipid concentration. The review also integrates the physiological rationale underlying lipid resuscitation and explores a mechanistically informed framework for interpreting formulation-specific effects of ILEs. A literature search of PubMed, Embase, and Google Scholar was conducted from January 1998 through January 2026. Twenty experimental studies were identified-nine in vitro, one ex vivo, and ten in vivo-and qualitatively synthesized according to their principal mechanisms of action, including lipid shuttle, cardiotonic, vascular, and metabolic effects. The available experimental evidence suggests that 100% LCT-containing ILEs provide greater overall cardiovascular recovery than 50% MCT/LCT-containing ILEs, particularly through more effective lipid-shuttle activity and sustained myocardial protection. Conversely, 50% MCT/LCT-containing ILEs demonstrated greater vascular effects in several experimental models. Evidence comparing lipid concentrations was limited to 100% LCT-containing formulations and generally showed greater pharmacokinetic, hemodynamic, and survival effects with a 30% versus a 20% lipid concentration when administered at the same volume. The available evidence is derived exclusively from heterogeneous preclinical experimental models and should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating rather than practice-informing. Triglyceride composition and lipid concentration may influence distinct mechanisms contributing to cardiovascular recovery during LAST. These findings provide a mechanistic basis for exploring formulation-phenotype associations but do not establish formulation-specific treatment recommendations. Further experimental and translational studies are needed to determine whether these mechanistic findings translate into clinically meaningful benefits in patients with LAST.

papers.abstract: Severe neurologic injury after uncomplicated general anesthesia in previously healthy patients is rare. Since 2021, reports from South America and later from North America and Europe have described catastrophic neurologic deterioration and death after routine general anesthesia in children and adults with Venezuelan maternal ancestry. A homoplasmic mitochondrial DNA variant, MT-ND4 m.11232 T > C (p.Leu158Pro), affecting complex I of the electron transport chain, has emerged as the leading candidate susceptibility factor. This systematic review identified, appraised, and synthesized available evidence linking inhaled anesthetics, in particular sevoflurane, with severe perioperative neurologic complications in carriers of this variant and in individuals with Venezuelan maternal ancestry. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261471143), with searches of major biomedical databases, gray literature, and variant databases. The evidence describes a consistent but incompletely characterized syndrome defined by maternal Venezuelan ancestry, apparent preoperative health, predominant sevoflurane exposure, delayed emergence, and severe basal ganglia injury with frequent death. In patient-derived fibroblasts and cybrids, sevoflurane markedly suppressed complex I-dependent respiration, whereas propofol did not. Incidence, penetrance, and agent-specific risk remain uncertain. Cautious perioperative strategies that avoid volatile anesthetics appear justified.

papers.abstract: The present study compared the effects of high-frequency oscillatory ventilation (HFOV) with automated volume guarantee (HFOV-VG) versus careful manual high-frequency tidal volume (VThf) monitoring (HFOV-VM) on the incidences of hypo/hypercarbia in neonates. In this open-labeled, parallel-group randomized controlled trial, 60 neonates failing conventional mechanical ventilation were allocated to receive HFOV-VG (n = 30) versus HFOV-VM (n = 30) as a rescue mode. The primary outcome was the incidence of hypo/hypercarbia at 1 h. Secondary outcomes were incidences of hypo/hypercarbia at 6/12/24/48 h and beyond, time-specific trends for partial pressure of carbon dioxide (pCO2), delivered VThf and mean airway pressure (MAP), cerebral blood flow (CBF) in the anterior cerebral artery (ACA) and regional cerebral oxygenation (CrSO2), duration of respiratory support, and incidences of in-hospital adverse events. Stata 18 was used for an intention-to-treat analysis. The incidence of hypo- or hypercarbia at 1 h of intervention was 15/30 (50%) in the HFOV-VG and 13/30 (43%) in the HFOV-VM groups (p = 0.61). No differences were observed in the incidences of hypo- or hypercarbia anytime during HFOV. Time-specific pCO2, VThf, and MAP were similar. On regression analysis, the only significant predictor for pCO2 at 1 h was the baseline pCO2 level in both the groups. No difference was observed in ACA-CBF, CrSO2, duration of respiratory support, and in-hospital adverse events including mortality. There was no difference in the incidence of hypo/hypercarbia with HFOV-VG versus HFOV-VM at 1 h and throughout the duration of ventilation with a similar rate of complications when used as a rescue therapy. papers.abstract: Postoperative hypotension can be caused by vasodilation, myocardial dysfunction, severe hypovolemia, and obstruction. We sought to estimate the effects of these causes on the incidence of hypotension after major vascular surgery. We conducted a single-centre prospective cohort study of male and female adult patients undergoing major vascular surgery. We conducted point-of-care ultrasound and sidestream darkfield microscopy imaging to detect vasodilation, myocardial dysfunction, severe hypovolemia, and obstruction. The primary outcome was hypotension (systolic blood pressure < 90 mm Hg or a vasopressor infusion) within 24 hr of surgery. We recruited 100 patients, of whom 89 had data available for analysis. Hypotension occurred in 20 participants (23%), vasodilation in 30 (34%), and myocardial dysfunction in 11 (12%). Severe hypovolemia and obstruction were not observed. The adjusted marginal risk difference of hypotension was 33% (95% confidence interval [CI], 14% to 53%; P < 0.001) for vasodilation and 41% (95% CI, 3% to 79%; P = 0.03) for myocardial dysfunction. Vasodilation increased the risk of intensive care unit admission by 27% (95% CI, 8% to 45%; P = 0.006) and of requiring a vasopressor infusion by 22% (95% CI, 4% to 39%; P = 0.02). Vasodilation and myocardial dysfunction increased the risk of postoperative hypotension, providing insight into the mechanistic development of postoperative hypotension. The absence of severe hypovolemia was surprising. Clinicians should assess for vasodilation and myocardial dysfunction as potential preludes to postoperative hypotension, potentially using point-of-care echocardiography and sidestream darkfield microscopy.

papers.abstract: ARDS comprises distinct inflammatory subphenotypes, including hyper- and hypo-inflammatory forms. Whether these differ in ventilation/perfusion (V/Q) mismatch and response to ventilatory strategies remains unclear. Dual-energy CT enables regional assessment of aeration and perfusion. This experimental study aimed to compare V/Q mismatch between hyper- and hypo-inflammatory subphenotypes, and respective responses to PEEP and prone positioning. In 10 pigs, hypo-inflammatory ARDS was induced by lung lavage followed by injurious ventilation. Hyper-inflammatory ARDS was produced by i.v. endotoxin infusion and fluid loading. Pigs were randomised to hypo- or hyperinflammatory ARDS, with similar oxygenation impairment. Dual-energy CT scans were obtained at individualised low, optimal, and high PEEP settings, in supine and prone positions. V/Q was derived from regional gas and blood volume and classified as low ( 2). Linear mixed-effects models included injury group, PEEP, and posture as fixed effects, and subject as a random effect. Hyper-inflammatory injury showed more severe V/Q mismatch than hypo-inflammatory injury (normal V/Q: 35% [sd=10] vs 51% [8] at low PEEP, supine position; P<0.01). Both PEEP optimisation and prone positioning improved V/Q. Prone positioning reduced high V/Q and dead space in hypo-inflammatory injury (group×posture interaction: F1,50=4.32, P=0.04), whereas PEEP reduced low V/Q and shunt in the supine position independent of ARDS subphenotype. In porcine models of hyper- and hypo-inflammatory ARDS, hyper-inflammatory injury was associated with more severe V/Q mismatch despite similar oxygenation. Distinct responses to PEEP and prone positioning support a subphenotype-tailored approach to ventilatory management.

papers.abstract: Canada faces mounting anesthesia workforce pressures, particularly in rural and smaller urban centres. Understanding residents' motivations regarding practice setting, research, and fellowship training is essential for workforce planning. We aimed to update a 2015 national survey to characterize current preferences and temporal shifts among Canadian anesthesiology residents. We conducted an anonymous, cross-sectional survey of residents in accredited Canadian anesthesiology programs (November-December 2024) using Research Electronic Data Capture. Items addressed demographics, practice setting, research experience and intentions, and fellowship plans. Selected responses were compared with 2015 survey items using Chi square tests and odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals; all tests used an alpha of 0.05. Ninety-four residents responded (12% response rate). Most preferred academic practice (63%), and half preferred to remain at their training institution (49%). Interest in rural practice was reported by 49%. Although research participation was common during medical school (94%) and residency (83%), only 18% intended to pursue research after residency. Approximately 63% intended to pursue fellowship training. Compared with the 2015 survey, there were significant increases in intention to remain at the same institution (from 35% to 50%; P = 0.02) and residency research participation (from 69% to 83%; P < 0.01), whereas intention to pursue research after residency declined (from 34% to 18%; P < 0.01). Canadian anesthesiology residents continue to favour academic practice and fellowship training, yet fewer plan to integrate research into future careers. These findings highlight opportunities for targeted mentorship, greater research autonomy, financial support, and expanded rural training pathways to align resident priorities with workforce needs.

papers.abstract: The solicitation of same-day consent for participation in clinical research is commonly prohibited by research ethics boards because of concerns about limited decision-making time and patient vulnerability. However, these concerns lack empirical support and restrict both research efforts and patient participation opportunities, particularly in medical specialties such as emergency medicine, critical care, and anesthesiology, in which clinicians and patients interact for the first time on the day of a procedure. We aimed to assess the voluntariness of research consent solicited on the day of surgery compared with consent obtained in advance. We performed a prospective, noninferiority randomized controlled trial examining the voluntariness of informed consent to participate in a low-risk clinical research trial at Women's College Hospital in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. The trial design included active deception (invitation to participate in a fabricated research trial) to capture authentic measurements of participants' perceptions of any perceived coercion. We randomized 114 patients scheduled to undergo anterior cruciate ligament repair for recruitment into a fabricated low-risk perioperative research trial at one of two time points: at a virtual preanesthesia clinic appointment in advance of the day of surgery, or on the day of surgery. Regardless of their decision, all participants received the (same) standard of care. Overall, 71/114 patients (62%) either consented to participate in the fabricated trial or declined participation but consented to a feedback session during which perceptions of coercion were assessed. Greater participation was observed among patients approached on the day of surgery (fabricated trial, 26/58 [45%]; feedback session only, 18/58 [31%]) than in advance (fabricated trial, 17/56 [30%]; feedback session only, 10/56 [18%]). Perceived coercion, measured using two validated psychometric instruments, did not differ between patients recruited on the day of surgery and those recruited in advance. A subset of patients in each group reported modest perceptions of undue influence, but regardless of recruitment time point, these patients demonstrated their agency to decline participation. Our findings suggest that restrictive same-day consent policies, when based on concerns regarding undue influence, may represent a structural barrier to participation in low-risk trials that lacks empirical justification. 1) Open Science Framework ( 46twc ); first submitted 17 March 2023; 2) ClinicalTrials.gov ( NCT07380035 ); first submitted 16 January 2026.

papers.abstract: Post-ICU care often misses patients unable to attend in-person clinic visits. Remote assessments of physical function might increase access to ICU aftercare. We investigated whether patient-reported disability predicts handgrip strength (HGS) and the 2-Minute Walk Test (2MWT) distance with sufficient clinical accuracy. This secondary analysis of the stepped-wedge cluster-randomised Enhanced Recovery after Intensive Care trial included patients from 10 German ICU clusters who completed the WHO Disability Assessment Schedule (WHODAS) 2.0 plus either HGS, the 2MWT, or both, 6 months after ICU discharge. Relationships between WHODAS 2.0, HGS, and 2MWT were analysed using scatter plots, correlation coefficients, linear regressions, and Bland-Altman plots. Predictions of HGS and the 2MWT were compared with the minimal clinically important difference (MCID) for both measures. Of 1463 enrolled patients, 620 were analysed. The median WHODAS 2.0 sum score was 11 (Q1, Q3: 3, 22). The median HGS, expressed as a percentage of the expected value (%exp), was 70.6%exp (Q1, Q3: 54.4, 85.6), and the median 2MWT distance was 73.7%exp (Q1, Q3: 61.5, 85.8). The 2MWT was not completed by 59% of patients. Higher disability was moderately correlated with lower HGS (Spearman %exp: -0.41) and shorter 2MWT distance (Spearman %exp: -0.47). In multivariable regression models, the WHODAS 2.0 sum score predicted HGS in kg (β: -0.27 [95% CI: -0.33 to -0.22]; P<0.001) and 2MWT distance in m (β: -1.94 [95% CI: -2.37 to -1.51]; P<0.001), but the limits of agreement exceeded the MCIDs. With increasing disability, HGS and 2MWT performance declined, although correlations were moderate and uncertainty of predictions exceeded MCIDs of both instruments. Remote WHODAS 2.0 assessments cannot replace in-person physical function testing. NCT03671447.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Interstage infants with single‐ventricle (SV) physiology following Stage I palliation represent a high‐risk population for noncardiac procedures requiring anesthesia. Data comparing perioperative outcomes by shunt type remain limited. Aims Describe anesthetic management, perioperative complications, and postoperative outcomes in interstage SV infants undergoing noncardiac interventions and compare outcomes between right ventricle‐to‐pulmonary artery (Sano) and modified Blalock‐Taussig‐Thomas shunt (mBTTS) patients. Methods We performed a retrospective single‐center cohort study of interstage SV infants with Stage I palliation undergoing noncardiac surgery or nonsurgical procedures requiring anesthesia between 2015 and 2023. Outcomes were stratified by shunt type. Results A total of 208 noncardiac interventions in 120 interstage SV infants were analyzed; 136 (65.4%) encounters in 86 Sano patients and 72 (34.6%) encounters in 34 mBTTS patients. Compared with mBTTS infants, Sano patients underwent interventions at a younger age (57 [IQR 40–83] vs. 105 [59–278] days, p < 0.001) and lower weight (3.6 [3.0–4.1] vs. 4.8 [3.4–7.3] kg, p < 0.001). mBTTS procedures had higher rates of ventricular dysfunction (34.3% vs. 12.7%, p < 0.001), chromosomal abnormalities (63.9% vs. 19.1%, p < 0.001), gastrointestinal comorbidities (87.5% vs. 72.1%, p = 0.014), and hematologic comorbidities (41.7% vs. 22.8%, p = 0.006). Hemodynamic instability requiring vasoactive support was the most common perioperative complication and occurred similarly between groups (31.9% mBTTS vs. 31.6% Sano, p = 0.962). There were no perioperative cardiac arrests. Rates of postoperative escalation of care (2.9%), reintubation (3.0% vs. 2.9%, p = 0.999), readmission (16.2% vs. 16.9%, p = 0.999), and 30‐day mortality (2.3% vs. 2.9%, p = 0.999) were low and comparable between groups. Conclusions Despite the high‐risk physiology of interstage SV patients, perioperative outcomes were comparable between Sano and mBTTS cohorts. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and should not imply low procedural risk. Favorable outcomes likely reflect careful patient selection, multidisciplinary perioperative care, and specialized institutional expertise.

papers.abstract: The erector spinae plane block (ESPB) is widely used for primary breast cancer surgery (BCS), though its clinical benefits within optimized multimodal analgesia pathways remain uncertain. Intravenous lidocaine infusion (IVLI) offers a simple, reproducible alternative with potential systemic analgesic effects. This randomized, tripleblinded, placebo controlled, twocentre trial compared the quality of recovery after ESPB versus IVLI for BCS. Eighty adult patients undergoing primary BCS, with or without axillary dissection, were randomized to receive either ultrasoundguided ESPB (n=40) or intraoperative IVLI (n=40), in addition to a standardized multimodal analgesic protocol. The primary outcome was quality of recovery (QoR15) score at 24 hours. Secondary outcomes included postoperative pain scores, opioid consumption, adverse events, and rescue analgesia requirements. Both interventions produced excellent postoperative recovery, with 24hour QoR15 scores approaching preoperative baselines with no significant difference between groups (mean (SD) 24-hour QoR score; ESPB vs. IVLI group, 137.7(17.9) vs. 136.3(8.8), p=0.61). Pain burden and analgesic requirements over the first 24 hours were similarly low, and no ESPB or lidocainerelated adverse events were observed. Within a standardized multimodal analgesic framework, postoperative recovery and analgesic outcomes did not differ significantly between IVLI and ESPB, suggesting that IVLI may offer a pragmatic alternative when regional anesthesia expertise is limited.

papers.abstract: Recovery after non-cardiac surgery increasingly occurs at home, where clinical deterioration may go unrecognized. Digital health interventions may extend postoperative surveillance beyond discharge, but vary widely in components and clinician involvement. We evaluated their association with readmission and other outcomes. Five databases were searched from inception to December 12, 2025, for prospective randomized and observational studies comparing digital health interventions with standard care in adults after non-cardiac surgery. Readmission was the primary outcome; all-cause and major complications, emergency room (ER) visits, length of stay (LOS), and patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) were secondary. Interventions were grouped by whether a clinician reviewed patient-submitted data and had the ability to take action (active clinician involvement). Random-effects models pooled risk ratios (RR), mean differences (MD), and standardized mean differences (SMD). p values were adjusted for multiple comparisons (Benjamini-Hochberg). In 38 studies (30 randomized, 8 observational; 7,494 patients), digital health interventions were associated with fewer readmissions (17 studies, n=3,944; RR 0.85, 95% CI 0.73-0.99, adjusted p=0.045), ER visits (RR 0.78, 95% CI 0.63-0.97), and major complications (RR 0.75, 95% CI 0.60-0.94), but not all-cause complications (RR 0.92, 95% CI 0.79-1.08) or LOS (MD -0.04 days, 95% CI -0.26 to 0.18). Pain and anxiety were lower and functional status, quality-of-life, and satisfaction scores higher (absolute SMD 0.41-0.69). Readmission risk was lower with active clinician involvement (RR 0.76, 95% CI 0.64-0.92) but not without it (RR 0.96, 95% CI 0.78-1.18; interaction p=0.029). Heterogeneity in interventions, cohorts, and outcomes was substantial (PROM I² 50-97%). Digital health interventions were associated with fewer readmissions, ER visits, major complications, and better PROMs, but not fewer all-cause complications or shorter LOS. The readmission association was concentrated in studies with active clinician involvement. Heterogeneity was substantial and certainty of evidence low to very low.

papers.abstract: Paratracheal air cysts are rare benign anatomical variants. Although case reports suggest that paratracheal air cysts may lead to complications such as difficult ventilation and pneumothorax in patients whose lungs are mechanically ventilated, their association with postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs) remains unclear. We hypothesized that the presence of cysts is associated with an increased incidence of PPCs. In the context of COVID-19, we conducted a retrospective study of all patients undergoing surgery under general anesthesia in 2020. On the basis of the presence of paratracheal air cysts, we divided patients into two groups: the paratracheal air cyst group and the paratracheal-air-cyst‑free group. The primary outcome was the incidence of PPCs. We used propensity score matching to adjust for confounding and performed multivariable logistic regression analysis in the matched cohort to assess the association. Among 7,208 patients, the prevalence of paratracheal air cysts was 2.0% (141/7,208). The incidence of PPCs was 22% (31/141) in the paratracheal air cyst group and 15% (43/280) in the paratracheal-air-cyst-free group. Multivariable regression analysis showed that, after adjusting for confounders, the presence of paratracheal air cysts was associated with an increased risk of PPCs (adjusted odds ratio, 1.85; 95% confidence interval, 1.03 to 3.33; P = 0.04). The presence of paratracheal air cysts was associated with an increased risk of PPCs. Although this association warrants cautious interpretation due to possible residual confounding and lack of data on intraoperative ventilatory settings, anesthesiologists should consider the potential perioperative implications of this anatomical abnormality during preoperative assessment.

papers.abstract: Given the fiduciary responsibility of an academic clinical department to ensure appropriate use of funds to support research, the Department of Anesthesia, Pain Management and Perioperative Medicine at Dalhousie University (Halifax, NS, Canada) aimed to create a framework to support the allocation of remunerated protected research time to clinician faculty members within the department. A departmental Research Accountability Project (RAP) was undertaken in the context of a quality improvement initiative. The RAP initially engaged clinician faculty members in the form of a survey, interviews, and a questionnaire to provide feedback regarding current practices for evaluating protected time for research. On the basis of this feedback, a working group created a list of 151 research outputs encompassing the breadth of research-related activities and assigned scores based on their relative merit. Clinicians with protected research time completed their academic profile, and individual point allocations were calculated. Scores were then weighted by different categories (e.g., publications, grant capture, presentations), and a RAP dashboard was developed to capture research outputs, assign scores, and generate a reporting/feedback mechanism for further analysis. Faculty members acknowledged the importance of clinicians having remunerated protected time to carry out research; nevertheless, there was scepticism with respect to how protected research time was managed. These data were then assessed by the working group, and using the RAP metric, individual researcher reports consisting of scores and recommendations were sent to the department head for final evaluation. These reports formed the basis of the researchers' annual academic performance review and consideration for continuance. The RAP scoring system provides an objective measure of remunerated protected research time for clinicians to assist in researcher accountability.

papers.abstract: Predicting difficult intubation is still challenging, even with videolaryngoscopy. Videolaryngoscopy (VL) shows the larynx during intubation. The modified Cormack-Lehane (CL) classification grades laryngeal visibility but can vary between observers. Deep learning uses neural networks for objective, real-time airway image evaluation. We aimed to evaluate a YOLOv8-based model for object detection to automate modified CL grade classification from VL images in patients undergoing elective surgery. In this prospective observational study, we developed a deep learning model using 346 VL images from 151 patients undergoing elective surgery. Two anesthesiologists classified images according to the modified CL system, and interobserver agreement was analysed using Cohen's kappa and weighted kappa. We split the data into training (80%), validation (10%), and test (10%) sets, with imbalance corrected via Albumentations augmentation. We evaluated the model results using sensitivity, specificity, and mean average precision with a 95% confidence interval (CI) and validated the model on 60 images not included in the training set. Interobserver agreement ranged from moderate (Cohen's kappa = 0.59; 95% CI, 0.53 to 0.66) to good (weighted kappa = 0.79; 95% CI, 0.75 to 0.84). In the test set, the overall recall rate was 0.87, and the specificity was 0.83. In the difficult intubation grades, recall and specificity were observed to be 0.79 (95% CI, 0.52 to 0.92) and 0.93 (95% CI, 0.78 to 0.98), respectively, for CL grade 2b, and 0.60 and 1.00, respectively, for CL grade 3. In the external validation data set (n = 60), the model achieved an overall accuracy of 0.767 with a recognition rate of 0.925 for clinically relevant CL grades 2b and 3. The YOLOv8-based model showed promising performance in classifying modified CL grades, particularly for clinically relevant difficult views (CL grades 2b-3). Nevertheless, wide CIs and limited external validation indicate uncertainty. The model may be considered an auxiliary tool rather than an independent decision system and requires further validation in larger, multicentre data sets.

papers.abstract: Summary Introduction Difficult tracheal intubation is associated with serious complications, including hypoxia, bradycardia and cardiac arrest. Neonates have increased physiologic vulnerability compared with older children, yet detailed data on management strategies and outcomes in neonates with difficult tracheal intubation remain limited. We hypothesised that clinicians have lower first‐attempt tracheal intubation success and higher complication rates for neonates compared with older children with difficult tracheal intubation. Methods We analysed the Pediatric Difficult Intubation Registry to determine tracheal intubation first attempt success and incidence of complications. We used logistic regression to identify variables associated with complications in neonates. Results During the study period, 6283 paediatric difficult tracheal intubations were recorded, including 420 neonates. First attempt success was lower for neonates (139/420, 33.1%) than older children (2394/4683, 51.1%). Complications occurred more frequently in neonates (123/420, 29.3%) than older children (637/4683, 13.6%). Hypoxia occurred in 92/420 (21.9%) neonates and 269/4683 (5.7%) older children. Severe complications were more frequent in neonates vs. older children (12/420, 2.9% vs. 30/4683, 0.6%, respectively), with cardiac arrests occurring in 4/420 (1.0%) neonates and 11/4683 (0.2%) older children. Difficult mask ventilation occurred more frequently in neonates (60/420, 14.3%) than older children (353/4681, 7.5%). In neonates, increased number of tracheal intubation attempts (aOR 1.61 per attempt, 95%CI 1.30–2.00, p < 0.001) and difficult facemask ventilation (aOR 3.17, 95%CI 1.38–7.30, p = 0.007) were associated with complications. Anticipated difficulty with airway management had a protective effect (aOR 0.37, 95%CI 0.16–0.88, p = 0.025). Discussion Neonates with difficult tracheal intubation experience a substantially higher rate of complications than older children. Early recognition of risk is critical in order to enable careful planning to minimise tracheal intubation attempts in this vulnerable population.

papers.abstract: Heart rate (HR) and arterial blood pressure (BP) monitoring is standard of care during paediatric anaesthesia, yet evidence-based reference values for anaesthetised children remain limited. Existing BP reference values do not account for the combined effects of age, sex, weight, and height, and HR reference values in this population are lacking. We conducted a retrospective multicentre study using data from the Multicenter Perioperative Outcomes Group anaesthesia registry (2016-22). Included patients were aged <18 yr, ASA physical status 1 or 2, and undergoing noncardiac procedures under general anaesthesia. We used quantile regression to model the 2.3rd, 16th, 50th, 84th, and 97.7th centiles for HR, mean arterial pressure (MAP), systolic BP, and diastolic BP at two time points: the preparation phase (end of induction) and surgical phase (15-35 min after procedure start). Model covariates included age, sex, weight, and height. We selected the best model for each outcome using cross-validation with pinball loss. A total of 284 385 patients from 57 institutions were analysed. Optimal model complexity varied by outcome: a two-way interaction model was selected as the best-performing model for preparation phase HR and surgical phase MAP. A three-way interaction model was selected as the best-performing model for the remaining outcomes. Comprehensive prediction tables and an interactive web-based tool were developed for all outcomes. This study provides integrated HR and BP reference values for healthy paediatric patients undergoing general anaesthesia, incorporating age, sex, weight, and height simultaneously. These reference values with an interactive website can support clinical decision-making and haemodynamic monitoring.

papers.abstract: Summary Introduction Videolaryngoscopy has been associated with improved glottic visualisation and higher first‐attempt tracheal intubation success compared with direct laryngoscopy. However, multicentre evidence evaluating its effectiveness when tracheal intubation is performed by anaesthesia resident doctors in routine practice is limited. Methods Adult patients undergoing surgery requiring tracheal intubation were assigned to videolaryngoscopy or direct laryngoscopy for the initial attempt. All tracheal intubations were performed by anaesthesia residents under consultant supervision. The primary outcome was successful tracheal intubation on the first attempt. Secondary outcomes included glottic visualisation; number of tracheal intubation attempts; need for adjunct airway devices; procedural difficulty; and procedural complications. Results We enrolled 1001 patients and assigned 501 to videolaryngoscopy and 500 patients to direct laryngoscopy. Successful first‐attempt tracheal intubation was achieved in 397 (79.2%) patients allocated to the videolaryngoscopy group and 351 (70.2%) patients allocated to the direct laryngoscopy group (absolute risk difference 9.0%, 95%CI 3.7–14.4%, p < 0.001). Videolaryngoscopy improved glottic visualisation, with more patients having a modified Cormack–Lehane grade 2 or 2a view (467/501 (93.3%) vs. 404/500 (80.8%); p < 0.001); decreased operator‐reported tracheal intubation difficulty (168/501 (33.5%) vs. 236/500 (47.2%); p < 0.001) and reduced procedural complications (39/501 (7.7%) vs. 91/500 (18.2%); p < 0.001), without a clinically meaningful difference in tracheal intubation time or the need for adjunct airway devices. Discussion In adult patients undergoing tracheal intubation by anaesthesia resident doctors, videolaryngoscopy increased first‐attempt success and improved overall procedural performance compared with direct laryngoscopy.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Intraoperative hypotension is a common complication in pediatric anesthesia. The definition of hypotension and treatment strategies are heterogeneous. The association of these treatments with cerebral regional oxygen saturation, measured by near‐infrared spectroscopy, is insufficiently characterized. Aims The study explores whether changes in cerebral regional oxygen saturation, mean arterial pressure, and heart rate differ after the administration of an isotonic fluid bolus, noradrenaline, adrenaline, or cafedrine/theodrenaline for perioperative hypotension in children. Methods This single‐center, observational pilot study included children aged 18 years or younger undergoing noncardiac surgery who developed hypotension requiring treatment. The choice of the intervention was at the discretion of the attending anesthetist and guided by an internal guideline. Cerebral regional oxygen saturation, mean arterial pressure, and heart rate were recorded for 8 min after the first intervention and analyzed relative to the value immediately before treatment. Groups were compared using the area under the curve of these changes and linear mixed‐effects models. Results Forty‐six patients were analyzed. Cerebral regional oxygen saturation immediately before treatment did not differ from the pre‐induction baseline. Cafedrine/theodrenaline was the only treatment associated with a sustained increase in cerebral regional oxygen saturation, with a significantly higher area under the curve than noradrenaline ( p = 0.017), adrenaline ( p = 0.017), and fluid administration ( p < 0.001), which was confirmed by mixed‐effects models. Only cafedrine/theodrenaline was associated with an increase in heart rate. Changes in heart rate were significantly correlated with changes in cerebral regional oxygen saturation (Spearman's ρ = 0.376, p = 0.010), but not with changes in mean arterial pressure. Conclusions Cafedrine/theodrenaline was associated with a sustained increase in cerebral regional oxygen saturation, heart rate, and blood pressure. Noradrenaline, adrenaline, and fluid administration were associated with unchanged or decreasing cerebral regional oxygen saturation. Randomized controlled studies are required to confirm these findings.

papers.abstract: Right-sided double-lumen endobronchial tubes (DLTs) are often avoided because of technical difficulties and concerns about respiratory complications, although evidence that they increase hypoxemia during anesthesia remains limited and inconsistent. We evaluated the association between DLT side and hypoxemia during anesthesia in patients undergoing unilateral surgery for left-sided lung tumors. This single-center retrospective cohort study included adult patients undergoing unilateral surgery for left-sided lung tumors between October 2008 and May 2023. The primary outcome was hypoxemia during anesthesia, defined as SpO2 ≤ 90% for at least 3 consecutive min during the anesthetic period. Propensity score overlap weighting was used to adjust for measured differences between patients receiving right-sided and left-sided DLTs. Odds ratios (ORs) and absolute risk differences (RDs) were estimated. Among 1,280 patients, 842 received right-sided DLTs and 438 received left-sided DLTs. After overlap weighting, measured covariates were well balanced. The incidence of hypoxemia during anesthesia was 20.0% with right-sided DLTs and 18.5% with left-sided DLTs (OR, 1.10; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.68-1.79; P = 0.70). The RD was 1.51 percentage points (95% CI - 3.86-6.87). No clear between-group differences were observed in exploratory secondary respiratory outcomes. We found no clear evidence that right-sided DLT use was associated with a higher incidence of hypoxemia during anesthesia than left-sided DLT use. However, equivalence between the two devices was not established, and further studies are needed to determine whether clinically important differences in hypoxemia risk exist.

papers.abstract: Postoperative pain management remains a critical issue in peri-operative medicine, but contemporary national data are lacking. AlgoSFAR 2 was a prospective, multicentre and observational study, conducted in randomly selected French surgical centres. Adult patients undergoing elective surgery were included. Pain was assessed at rest and during mobilization over the first three postoperative days. Secondary outcomes included postoperative opioid consumption and multimodal analgesia strategies defined as the use of at least two non-opioid strategies such as analgesics and/or regional anaesthesia. A total of 3879 patients from 80 centres were analysed. While pre-operative and immediate postoperative pain levels at rest were low, pain peaked on day 1, with high interindividual variability, and 6% of patients reported severe pain. Two thirds (66%) did not need any rescue opioids postoperatively. Overall, 95% received multimodal analgesia. These results highlight a major change in postoperative pain management in France, with broad adoption of multimodal opioid-sparing strategies. Nonetheless, a minority of patients still experience severe pain, highlighting the need for personalized management. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06487442.

papers.abstract: In severe postpartum haemorrhage (PPH), hypofibrinogenaemia is strongly associated with bleeding severity. To correct fibrinogen depletion, various fixed dosing regimens have been evaluated, but the optimal fibrinogen dosing regimen remains unknown. To date, fibrinogen pharmacokinetics have only been studied outside haemorrhagic settings (healthy or afibrinogenaemic patients) METHODS: This ancillary analysis of the TRACES trial assessed fibrinogen kinetics in 142 women with PPH > 800 ml during caesarean section, among which 31 received fibrinogen replacement. Plasma fibrinogen concentrations (n = 593) were measured using the Clauss method. A population pharmacokinetic model was developed using nonlinear mixed-effects modeling. Simulations were performed to estimate loading and maintenance doses required to achieve target fibrinogen concentrations. A one-compartment logistic model adequately described plasma fibrinogen levels. Bleeding rate was identified as a key covariate to explain fibrinogen loss rate. Based on the estimated model, an optimised dosing regimen was derived to achieve and maintain predefined target fibrinogen levels. To achieve a target increase of 1 g.L-¹ in plasma fibrinogen level, the required fibrinogen loading dose is at least 2.7 g for a body weight of 50 kg. To maintain plasma fibrinogen level at a target of 2 g.L-¹ during a 1000 mL.h-¹ bleeding rate, a fibrinogen infusion rate of 0.9 g.h-¹ would be required. This work supports that an individualized target-controlled fibrinogen dosing strategy is probably required to effectively correct fibrinogen levels. Integrating such models as a clinical decision support tool into a multimodal strategy that also utilizes viscoelastic testing could optimize PPH management.

papers.abstract: A meta-analysis in a recent issue of the British Journal of Anaesthesia pools randomised evidence on intraoperative arterial blood pressure targets in nine trials in noncardiac surgery. With a total of 14 658 patients included in the analysis, the authors show that higher mean arterial pressure targets do not reduce 30-day mortality, acute kidney injury, or myocardial injury. These findings reinforce the distinction between low blood pressure as a marker of perioperative vulnerability and low blood pressure as a modifiable therapeutic target. Correcting arterial pressure might normalise a number without removing the underlying physiological vulnerability that drives adverse postoperative outcomes. Therefore, this meta-analysis supports a shift from reflexive increases in blood pressure targets towards attention to the underlying cause of haemodynamic instability.

papers.abstract: Whether targeting an individualized mean arterial pressure (MAP) during cardiac surgery improves outcomes remains uncertain. The balance between improved perfusion and vasopressor-driven blood pressure augmentation is unclear. In this single-blind, multicenter randomized clinical trial conducted in 10 tertiary centers in France, adult patients undergoing elective cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass were assigned to either individualized MAP management (target within ±10% of preoperative baseline during surgery and for 24 h postoperatively) or standard management (target MAP ≥65 mm Hg). The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause death, acute kidney injury, or prespecified neurologic complications within 7 days. Safety outcomes included hemorrhagic complications and transfusion requirements. A total of 172 patients were enrolled before the trial was stopped early by the data and safety monitoring board because of increased bleeding in the individualized group. Mean intraoperative MAP was higher with individualized management (80.6 vs 75.6 mm Hg; P<0.001), despite limited target adherence (33% of intraoperative time) and greater vasopressor use. The primary outcome occurred in 27 of 85 patients (32%) in the individualized group and 25 of 87 (29%) in the standard group (relative risk, 1.1; 95% CI, 0.7 to 1.8; P=0.76). Hemorrhagic complications occurred more frequently in the individualized group (18% vs 3%; P=0.003). In patients undergoing cardiac surgery, it was not possible to determine whether an individualized MAP strategy reduced major postoperative complications. More bleeding complications were observed in the individualized group. Future studies should further investigate this safety signal when evaluating individualized blood pressure targets.

papers.abstract: Accurate endotracheal tube (ETT) sizing is essential in pediatric airway management to optimize ventilation and reduce complications. Traditional methods, including age-based formulas and distal phalanx width (DPW), may lack precision. Subglottic ultrasound (US) has emerged as a promising tool, but its predictive accuracy compared with DPW remains unclear. This study aimed to compare accuracy, agreement, diagnostic performance, and clinical applicability of subglottic US versus DPW for predicting optimal ETT size in children, while recognizing that the enrolled cohort was predominantly school-aged. In this prospective observational study, pediatric patients aged 0-12 years undergoing elective or emergency intubation were assessed. Pre-intubation measurements included subglottic transverse airway diameter by ultrasound (ACUSON Juniper, microconvex probe, 5-10 MHz) and DPW by digital calipers. Predicted ETT sizes were compared with the final clinically accepted cuffed ETT inner diameter confirmed by leak testing and cuff pressure optimization. Agreement was evaluated using Bland-Altman analysis and intraclass correlation coefficients, while diagnostic performance was defined a priori as accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), likelihood ratios, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Logistic regression identified predictors of good ETT fit. Among 160 patients, the median age was 8.8 years (IQR 7.0-10.5), indicating predominance of older children. Ultrasound-predicted ETT size showed a stronger correlation with actual size (r = 0.479, p < 0.001) than DPW (r = 0.248, p = 0.002). Ultrasound predictions had narrower Bland-Altman limits of agreement, although ultrasound measurement is operator-dependent. DPW showed poor sensitivity (5.9%) but high specificity (99.3%) for identifying underfit ETTs, with limited overall discrimination (ROC AUC = 0.53). Only subglottic diameter was a significant predictor of good ETT fit. Subglottic ultrasound showed better agreement with clinically accepted ETT size than DPW in this predominantly school-aged pediatric cohort. These findings support the potential role of ultrasound as an adjunct to pediatric airway assessment, but conclusions should be interpreted cautiously in infants and younger children because they were under-represented. Standardized measurement protocols and operator training are needed before broad implementation.
